claims.quote: in the legend surrounding the formation of Lough Neagh, was a woman turned mermaid who inhabited the area before the great lake gushed up on dry land.

claims.statement: Family drowned; a year in an underwater chamber; became half human, half salmon.
claims.statement_id: Keluarga tenggelam; setahun di ruang bawah air; menjadi setengah manusia setengah salem.
claims.quote: Her family was drowned, but she survived in an underwater chamber in the lake for a year, after which she was transformed into a being who was half-human, half-salmon.

claims.statement: Baptised by St. Comgall: Muirgein/Muirgeilt; Saint Muirgen, 27 January; messenger to Rome; Inbhear nOllarbha (Larne Lough).
claims.statement_id: Dibaptis Comgall (St. Comgall): Muirgein/Muirgeilt; Santo (Saint) Muirgen, 27 Januari (January); utusan ke Roma (Rome); Inbhear nOllarbha (Larne Lough).
claims.quote: There she was baptised by Comgall, and given the Christened name Muirgein ("sea-born") or Muirgeilt ("sea-wander") . She appears as Saint Muirgen in genealogies of Irish saints with her feast day assigned to 27 January.

claims.statement: Annals of the Four Masters: captured 558 AD.
claims.statement_id: Annals of the Four Masters: ditangkap 558 M (A.D.).
claims.quote: Liban, a mermaid (muirgelt) who was the daughter of Eochaid, was captured in the year 558 A.D. according to the Annals of the Four Masters

claims.statement: Aided Echach maic Maireda, 12th-century Lebor na hUidre; Lough Neagh named after her father Eochaid mac Mairidh.
claims.statement_id: Aided Echach maic Maireda, Lebor na hUidre abad ke-12; Lough Neagh dinamai menurut ayahnya Eochaid mac Mairidh.
claims.quote: According to this old tale, Liban turned into a mermaid when a spring burst under her house to form Lough Neagh (Old Irish: Loch nEchach ), named after Liban's father Eochaid mac Mairidh who was drowned by the gushing water.

claims.statement: fi article: Liban chose heaven, was baptised and died.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fi: Liban memilih surga, dibaptis, lalu meninggal.
claims.quote: Liban valitsi taivaan, otti kasteen ja kuoli.

description.en: Likho, liho, lykho (Belarusian: лі́ха, Polish: licho, Russian: Лихо, Ukrainian: Лихо) is an embodiment of evil fate and misfortune in Slavic mythology. A creature with one eye who is often depicted as an old, skinny woman in black (Лихо одноглазое, One-eyed Likho) or as an evil male goblin of forests. Rather than being included in the major canon of the Slavic belief system, the Likho is traditionally found in fairy tales.

claims.statement: Likho (Polish licho) embodies evil fate and misfortune in Slavic mythology, a one-eyed creature often shown as a skinny old woman in black (One-eyed Likho) or an evil male forest goblin.
claims.statement_id: Likho (Лихо, Polandia licho) adalah perwujudan nasib buruk dan kemalangan dalam mitologi Slavia, makhluk bermata satu yang sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua kurus berpakaian hitam (Likho Bermata Satu) atau goblin hutan laki-laki yang jahat.
claims.quote: is an embodiment of evil fate and misfortune in Slavic mythology. A creature with one eye who is often depicted as an old, skinny woman in black (Лихо одноглазое, One-eyed Likho) or as an evil male goblin of forests.

claims.statement: Likho is traditionally found in fairy tales rather than the major canon of Slavic belief.
claims.statement_id: Likho secara tradisional ditemukan dalam dongeng, bukan dalam kanon utama kepercayaan Slavia.
claims.quote: Rather than being included in the major canon of the Slavic belief system, the Likho is traditionally found in fairy tales.

claims.statement: Likho cheats a person and rides on their neck; wanting to drown it, the person jumps into a river and drowns, while Likho floats away after other victims.
claims.statement_id: Likho menipu seseorang dan menunggang di lehernya; orang yang ingin menenggelamkannya melompat ke sungai dan malah tenggelam, sementara Likho mengapung keluar untuk mengejar korban lain.
claims.quote: Likho cheats a person and rides on their neck. The person wanting to drown Likho jumps into a river and drowns themself, but Likho floats out to chase other victims.

claims.statement: In superstition Likho was supposed to come and eat a person, used especially to scare small children; there are also tales of a person finally cheating Likho.
claims.statement_id: Dalam takhayul, Likho dikatakan datang dan memakan orang, dan ini dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak kecil; ada juga kisah manusia yang akhirnya menipu Likho.
claims.quote: Within the framework of superstitions, Likho was supposed to come and eat a person. In particular, this was used to scare small children.

claims.statement: In Russian likho means "evil, misfortune", originally "leftover, superfluous"; in tales Likho is often linked with Gore (Grief) and brings all kinds of misfortune to those it is near.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Rusia, likho berarti "kejahatan, kemalangan", dengan makna asal "sisa, berlebih"; dalam dongeng Likho sering dikaitkan dengan Gore (Duka) dan membawa berbagai kemalangan kepada orang yang didekatinya.
claims.quote: Лихо в русском языке — «зло, несчастье», в первоначальном значении — «остаточный, лишний».

claims.statement: In the Russian folk tale "One-eyed Likho" it appears as a thin, one-eyed, man-eating giantess.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng rakyat Rusia "Likho Bermata Satu", Likho tampil sebagai raksasa perempuan kurus bermata satu pemakan manusia.
claims.quote: В русской народной сказке «Лихо одноглазое» предстаёт в образе худой одноглазой великанши-людоедки.

claims.statement: Likho is not a real proper name but a noun meaning bad luck in modern Russian and Ukrainian.
claims.statement_id: Likho bukan nama diri, melainkan kata benda yang berarti nasib buruk dalam bahasa Rusia dan Ukraina modern.
claims.quote: Likho is not a real proper name but a noun meaning bad luck in modern Russian and Ukrainian

description.en: Litr (also Lit; Old Norse: [ˈlitz̠], 'colour, appearance') is the name borne by a dwarf and a jötunn in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: Litr (also Lit; Old Norse 'colour, appearance') is the name of a dwarf and a jötunn in Norse mythology.
claims.statement_id: Litr (juga Lit; Nordik Kuno, "warna, rupa") adalah nama seorang kurcaci dan seorang jötunn dalam mitologi Nordik.
claims.quote: Litr (also Lit; Old Norse: [ˈlitz̠] , 'colour, appearance') is the name borne by a dwarf and a jötunn in Norse mythology.

claims.statement: In Snorri Sturluson's Gylfaginning (49) Thor kicks Litr into Baldr's funeral pyre: as Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir, a dwarf named Litr ran before his feet, and Thor kicked him into the fire, where he burned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Gylfaginning (49) karya Snorri Sturluson, Litr ditendang Thor ke api pembakaran jenazah Baldr: Thor menyucikan api dengan Mjöllnir, seorang kurcaci bernama Litr berlari di depan kakinya, lalu Thor menendangnya ke api dan ia terbakar.
claims.quote: In Snorri Sturluson's Gylfaginning (49), Litr is kicked into Baldr's funeral pyre by Thor: ... Then Thor stood by and hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir; and before his feet ran a certain dwarf which was named Litr; Thor kicked at him with his foot and thrust him into the fire, and he burned.

claims.statement: The Old Norse name Litr has been translated 'colour', 'hue' or 'appearance', from a reconstructed Proto-Germanic *ulituz.
claims.statement_id: Nama Nordik Kuno Litr diterjemahkan "warna", "corak", atau "rupa", dan berasal dari bentuk Proto-Jermanik yang direkonstruksi *ulituz.
claims.quote: The Old Norse name Litr has been translated as 'colour', 'hue', or 'appearance'. It stems from a Proto-Germanic form reconstructed as *ulituz

claims.statement: Litr is also listed as a dwarf in Völuspá (12), and a dwarf Litr appears in Áns saga bogsveigis, forced by the hero Án to build him a bow.
claims.statement_id: Litr juga tercantum sebagai kurcaci dalam Völuspá (12), dan kurcaci bernama Litr muncul dalam Áns saga bogsveigis, dipaksa tokoh utama Án membuatkan busur.
claims.quote: Litr is also listed as a dwarf in Völuspá (12). A dwarf named Litr also appears in Áns saga bogsveigis, where he is coerced by the protagonist Án to build him a bow.

claims.statement: In a stanza by the skald Bragi Boddason quoted by Snorri in the Skáldskaparmál, Litr appears in a kenning for Thor, 'challenger of Lit's men' (Litar flotna fangboði); as Thor is the giants' enemy, Litr here is generally taken as a giant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bait skald Bragi Boddason yang dikutip Snorri dalam Skáldskaparmál, Litr disebut dalam kenning untuk Thor, "penantang tarung orang-orang Lit" (Litar flotna fangboði); karena Thor musuh para raksasa, Litr di sini umumnya dianggap raksasa.
claims.quote: En una estrofa del escaldo Bragi Boddason citada por Snorri en Skáldskaparmál Litr es también mencionado en un kenning para Thor: «El que desafía a luchar a los hombres de Lit» («Litar flotna fangboði»). Dado que Thor es el enemigo de los gigantes, generalmente se asume que, en este kenningar, Litr debe hacer referencia a un gigante.

claims.statement: This led John Lindow to suggest there was probably only one original Litr, a giant.
claims.statement_id: Hal ini membuat John Lindow menduga bahwa semula mungkin hanya ada satu Litr, seorang raksasa.
claims.quote: Esto llevó a John Lindow a sugerir que probablemente hubiera solo un Litr original, un gigante

description.en: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Welsh for 'Water Leaper') is an evil creature from Welsh folklore that lived in swamps and ponds. It is described as a giant frog with a bat's wings and zero legs whatsoever, and a long, lizard-like tail with a stinger at the end. It jumps across the water using its wings, hence its name. It was blamed for problems ranging from snapping fishing lines to eating livestock or even fishermen.

claims.statement: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Welsh for Water Leaper) is an evil creature of Welsh folklore of swamps and ponds.
claims.statement_id: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Wales/Welsh: Water Leaper, Pelompat Air) makhluk jahat cerita rakyat Wales, di rawa dan kolam; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Llamhigyn y Dŵr (Welsh for 'Water Leaper') is an evil creature from Welsh folklore that lived in swamps and ponds.

claims.statement: A giant frog with bat's wings, no legs, a lizard tail with a sting; leaps over water on its wings.
claims.statement_id: Katak raksasa bersayap kelelawar, tanpa kaki, ekor kadal bersengat; melompat di air dengan sayap.
claims.quote: It is described as a giant frog with a bat's wings and zero legs whatsoever, and a long, lizard-like tail with a stinger at the end. It jumps across the water using its wings, hence its name.

claims.statement: Blamed for snapped fishing lines and eaten livestock and fishermen.
claims.statement_id: Disalahkan atas putusnya tali pancing, dimakannya ternak dan nelayan.
claims.quote: It was blamed for problems ranging from snapping fishing lines to eating livestock or even fishermen.

claims.statement: A giant frog (grenouille géante) with bat (chauve-souris) wings for forelegs, no hind legs, a stinging lizard (lézard) tail.
claims.statement_id: Katak raksasa (grenouille géante), sayap kelelawar (chauve-souris) menggantikan kaki depan, tanpa kaki belakang, ekor kadal (lézard) bersengat.
claims.quote: Il est décrit comme une grenouille géante avec des ailes de chauve-souris à la place des pattes avant, sans pattes arrière et avec une longue queue de lézard avec un dard à la fin.

claims.statement: Per the es article the Saltador de agua (Llamhigyn Y Dwr) is a creature of Welsh (Gales) folklore of swamps and ponds.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel es, Saltador de agua (Llamhigyn Y Dwr) makhluk folklore Wales (Gales) di rawa dan kolam.
claims.quote: El Saltador de agua, también conocido como Llamhigyn Y Dwr, es una criatura del folclore de Gales que vivía en pantanos y charcas.

claims.statement: It breaks fishing lines, eats livestock and sometimes fishermen (pêcheurs).
claims.statement_id: Memutuskan tali pancing, memakan ternak dan kadang nelayan (pêcheurs).
claims.quote: Il provoque la rupture des lignes de pêche, mange du bétail et parfois des pêcheurs.

description.en: Across the Caribbean and African Disapora, the Loogaroo, Ligaroo, Lougarou or Lagahoo is a type of shapeshifter, sorcerer or vampire, similar to a werewolf. The term comes from the French word for werewolf, loup-garou. It is related to the myth of the Soucouyant.

claims.statement: Across the Caribbean and the African diaspora, the Loogaroo, Ligaroo, Lougarou or Lagahoo is a kind of shapeshifter, sorcerer or vampire similar to a werewolf.
claims.statement_id: Di Karibia dan diaspora Afrika, Loogaroo, Ligaroo, Lougarou, atau Lagahoo adalah sejenis pengubah wujud, penyihir, atau vampir yang mirip manusia serigala.
claims.quote: Across the Caribbean and African Disapora, the Loogaroo, Ligaroo, Lougarou or Lagahoo is a type of shapeshifter, sorcerer or vampire, similar to a werewolf.

claims.statement: The term comes from the French word for werewolf, loup-garou, and is related to the myth of the Soucouyant.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari kata Prancis untuk manusia serigala, loup-garou, dan berkaitan dengan mitos Soucouyant.
claims.quote: The term comes from the French word for werewolf, loup-garou. It is related to the myth of the Soucouyant.

claims.statement: In some myths, like the Soucouyant, the Loogaroo is a witch who sold her soul to the Devil and can shed her skin to become a vampiric fireball called a "corpse candle".
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian mitos, seperti Soucouyant, Loogaroo adalah penyihir perempuan yang menjual jiwanya kepada Iblis dan dapat melepas kulitnya untuk menjadi bola api pengisap darah yang disebut "corpse candle".
claims.quote: In some myths, like the Soucouyant, the Loogaroo is described as a witch who has sold her soul to the Devil. She is able to shed her skin to turn into a vampiric fireball, known as a "corpse candle".

claims.statement: According to these myths she keeps her magic only if she gives the Devil blood every night.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos ini, ia hanya punya kekuatan sihir bila memberi Iblis darah setiap malam.
claims.quote: According to these myths, she will have magical abilities only if she gives the Devil blood every night.

claims.statement: She leaves her skin, usually under a "Devil Tree", a silk cotton tree, and becomes a flame or bright blue ball of light that roams the night seeking blood.
claims.statement_id: Ia meninggalkan kulitnya, biasanya di bawah "pohon Iblis" yaitu pohon kapuk, lalu menjadi nyala api atau bola cahaya biru yang berkeliaran malam hari mencari darah.
claims.quote: The Loogahoo can leave her own skin (usually under a "Devil Tree," a silk cotton tree) and turn into a flame or blue ball of bright light that haunts the night searching for blood

claims.statement: In later versions Loogahoo is a man corrupted by wealth who has made a pact with the Devil to keep his status.
claims.statement_id: Dalam adaptasi yang lebih baru, Loogahoo adalah lelaki yang dirusak kekayaan dan bersekutu dengan Iblis untuk mempertahankan kedudukannya.
claims.quote: In later adaptations of the myth, Loogahoo is a man that has been corrupted by wealth and has dealt with the Devil to keep his status.

claims.statement: In Haiti the lougawou is a human, usually female, who turns into an animal and drains blood from sleeping victims.
claims.statement_id: Di Haiti, lougawou adalah manusia, biasanya perempuan, yang berubah menjadi hewan dan mengisap darah korban yang tidur.
claims.quote: In Haiti, the lougawou is a human, usually female, who transforms into an animal and drains blood from sleeping victims.

claims.statement: In Trinidad and Tobago the Lagahoo appears at night as a man with a coffin on his neck instead of a head, with three lit candles on top.
claims.statement_id: Di Trinidad dan Tobago, Lagahoo pada malam hari tampak sebagai lelaki yang lehernya memikul peti mati alih-alih kepala, dengan tiga lilin menyala di atasnya.
claims.quote: At night, he is described as taking the appearance of a man with a coffin on his neck instead of a head, atop which are three lit candles.

claims.statement: To defeat him he must be struck repeatedly with a stick soaked in holy water and holy oils for nine days.
claims.statement_id: Untuk mengalahkannya, ia harus dipukul berulang kali dengan tongkat yang dibasahi air suci dan minyak suci selama sembilan hari.
claims.quote: To defeat him, he must be repeatedly struck with a stick doused in holy water and holy oils for nine days.

claims.statement: In Mauritian folklore the Lougarou is a notorious figure used mostly to scare children; it appears at full moon and brings trouble to the locals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Mauritius, Lougarou adalah tokoh terkenal yang dipakai menakuti anak-anak; ia muncul saat bulan purnama dan membawa masalah bagi penduduk.
claims.quote: In Mauritian folklore, the Lougarou is a notorious figure mostly used to scare children. It appears at full moon and brings trouble to the local population.

description.en: The lubber fiend, Lob, lubberkin, lurdane or Lob Lie-By-The-Fire is a legendary creature of English folklore that is similar to the "brownie" (or "Urisk") of Scotland and northern England, the "hob" of northern England and the Scottish Borders, the Slavic "domovoi" and Scandinavian "tomte". It has been related also to Robin Goodfellow, and Hobgoblins. It is best known for being mentioned by John Milton in his pastoral poem, "L'Allegro". The lubberkin is typically described as a large, hairy man with a tail who performs housework in exchange for a saucer of milk and a place in front of the fire. One story claims he is the giant son of a witch and the Devil. The abbey lubber is a minor demon that haunts the wine cellars and kitchens of abbeys, tempting the monks into drunkenness, gluttony and lasciviousness. The best known abbey lubber tale is that of Friar Rush.

claims.statement: Lubber fiend (Lob, lubberkin, lurdane, Lob Lie-By-The-Fire), English folklore; like the brownie/Urisk of Scotland, hob, Slavic domovoi, Scandinavian tomte; Robin Goodfellow; mentioned by John Milton in L'Allegro.
claims.statement_id: Lubber fiend (Lob, lubberkin, lurdane, Lob Lie-By-The-Fire), folklor Inggris (English); mirip brownie/Urisk Skotlandia, hob, domovoi Slavia, tomte Skandinavia; Robin Goodfellow; disebut John Milton dalam L'Allegro.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature of English folklore that is similar to the "brownie" (or "Urisk") of Scotland and northern England, the "hob" of northern England and the Scottish Borders, the Slavic "domovoi" and Scandinavian "tomte". It has been related also to Robin Goodfellow, and Hobgoblins. It is best known for being mentioned by John Milton in his pastoral poem, "L'Allegro".

claims.statement: Large hairy tailed man doing housework for milk and a place by the fire.
claims.statement_id: Lelaki besar berbulu berekor, bekerja demi susu dan tempat di depan perapian.
claims.quote: The lubberkin is typically described as a large, hairy man with a tail who performs housework in exchange for a saucer of milk and a place in front of the fire.

claims.statement: Giant son of a witch and the Devil; the abbey lubber, a minor demon of abbeys.
claims.statement_id: Putra raksasa penyihir dan Iblis (Devil); abbey lubber setan kecil di biara.
claims.quote: One story claims he is the giant son of a witch and the Devil. The abbey lubber is a minor demon that haunts the wine cellars and kitchens of abbeys, tempting the monks into drunkenness, gluttony and lasciviousness.

claims.statement: In The Red Axe by S. R. Crockett (1900).
claims.statement_id: Dalam The Red Axe karya S. R. Crockett (1900).
claims.quote: The lubber fiend appears also in The Red Axe by S. R. Crockett (1900): That fool, Jan Lubber Fiend, will ever be at his tricks.

claims.statement: Edward Thomas's poem Lob; Lob Lie-By-The-Fire (Juliana H. Ewing); Dear Brutus (J. M. Barrie).
claims.statement_id: Puisi Lob karya Edward Thomas; Lob Lie-By-The-Fire (Juliana H. Ewing); Dear Brutus (J. M. Barrie).
claims.quote: Lob is the title of a poem by Edward Thomas. It also appears in Lob Lie-By-The-Fire by Juliana H. Ewing, Troll Fell by Katherine Langrish, Abbeychurch by Charlotte M. Yonge and Dear Brutus by J. M. Barrie

claims.statement: fr article: the Abbey Lubber is a minor demon of abbey wine cellars and kitchens; Friar Rush.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: Abbey Lubber setan kecil penghuni gudang anggur dan dapur biara; Friar Rush.
claims.quote: L'Abbey Lubber est un démon mineur qui hante les caves à vin et les cuisines des abbayes

claims.statement: A lubberkin in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt as a protective household spirit.
claims.statement_id: Lubberkin dalam The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt sebagai roh pelindung rumah.
claims.quote: A creature called a lubberkin appears in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, in which it is a type of protective household spirit

description.en: The Luison (Paraguayan Guaraní: Luisõ; Spanish: Luisón or Lobizón) is one of the seven legendary beasts of Paraguay, and is the seventh and last son of Tau and Kerana. The myth is known also in Argentina and says that in a family with seven male children, the last child will become Luisón.

claims.statement: The Luisón (Paraguayan Guarani Luisõ; Spanish Luisón or Lobizón) is one of the seven legendary beasts of Paraguay, the seventh and last son of Tau and Kerana; the myth is also known in Argentina and holds that in a family of seven sons the last will become a Luisón.
claims.statement_id: Luisón (Guarani Paraguay: Luisõ; Spanyol: Luisón atau Lobizón) adalah satu dari tujuh binatang legendaris Paraguay, putra ketujuh dan terakhir Tau dan Kerana; mitos ini juga dikenal di Argentina dan menyebut bahwa dalam keluarga dengan tujuh anak laki-laki, anak terakhir akan menjadi Luisón.
claims.quote: The Luison (Paraguayan Guaraní: Luisõ; Spanish: Luisón or Lobizón) is one of the seven legendary beasts of Paraguay, and is the seventh and last son of Tau and Kerana. The myth is known also in Argentina and says that in a family with seven male children, the last child will become Luisón.

claims.statement: In the original myth, as the seventh child of Tau and Kerana he was the most accursed, looking like a giant, hideous dog.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi asli, sebagai anak ketujuh Tau dan Kerana ia paling terkutuk, tampak seperti anjing raksasa yang sangat buruk rupa.
claims.quote: In the original version of the myth, Luisón was the seventh and last child of Tau and Kerana, and thus was the most accursed. He appeared to be a giant dog, and was said to be extremely ugly, even horrendous looking.

claims.statement: The myth says a family's seventh son will transform on his 13th birthday.
claims.statement_id: Mitos menyebut anak laki-laki ketujuh dalam keluarga akan berubah pada ulang tahunnya yang ke-13.
claims.quote: The myth tells that the seventh son in a family will transform on his 13th birthday.

claims.statement: The maned wolf, a slender long-legged wolf-like canid with a shambling gait, fitted the werewolf image brought by settlers and was eventually blended with local Guarani myths.
claims.statement_id: Serigala surai, anjing liar ramping berkaki panjang yang berjalan terseok, cocok dengan gambaran manusia serigala yang dibawa pendatang dan akhirnya berpadu dengan mitos Guarani setempat.
claims.quote: The maned wolf, a slender, wolf-like, stilted canid that moves with shambling steps, fitted the popular depiction of the werewolf and ultimately it was syncretized with local guarani myths.

claims.statement: Since the 19th century the President of Argentina has customarily been godparent to every seventh son, a custom born because superstitious people sometimes sacrificed their seventh son for fear he was a Luisón.
claims.statement_id: Sejak abad ke-19 Presiden Argentina biasa menjadi wali baptis setiap anak laki-laki ketujuh, kebiasaan yang muncul karena orang yang percaya takhayul kadang mengorbankan anak ketujuh mereka karena takut ia Luisón.
claims.quote: It has been customary since the 19th century for the President of Argentina to be named the "godparent" of each seventh male child of a married couple. This custom arose because superstitious people sometimes sacrificed their seventh son out of fear of the "possibility" that a Luisón had been born.

claims.statement: On 12 March 1973 President Juan Domingo Perón made the custom law through Decree No. 848, the presidential sponsorship law.
claims.statement_id: Pada 12 Maret 1973 Presiden Juan Domingo Perón meresmikan kebiasaan ini lewat Dekret No. 848, yang dikenal sebagai undang-undang perwalian presiden.
claims.quote: On 12 March 1973, President Juan Domingo Perón gave legal form to this custom through Decree No. 848, known as the presidential sponsorship law.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, as the seventh son of Tau and Keraná he bears his parents' heaviest curse; his very name terrifies, and he stands at the crossroads of life and death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, sebagai putra ketujuh Tau dan Keraná ia menanggung kutukan terberat orang tuanya; namanya saja menakutkan, dan ia berada di persimpangan jalan kehidupan dan kematian.
claims.quote: Luisón es el séptimo hijo de Tau y Keraná en la mitología guaraní, sobre él cayó la mayor maldición que pesaba sobre los progenitores. Su solo nombre aterroriza. Este ser espeluznante se encuentra ubicado en la encrucijada de los caminos de la vida y de la muerte.

claims.statement: According to the Portuguese article it is believed to look like a South American wolf or a red-eyed monkey, with fish fins and a huge tapir-like phallus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Portugis, ia dipercaya mirip serigala Amerika Selatan atau monyet bermata merah, bersirip ikan, dan berzakar besar seperti tapir.
claims.quote: Acredita-se que seja semelhante a um lobo sul-americano ou a um macaco de olhos vermelhos, com barbatanas de peixe e um enorme falo (de anta).

claims.statement: On full-moon nights falling on Friday and/or Tuesday the person turned into a half-animal creature.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam bulan purnama hari Jumat atau Selasa, orang itu berubah menjadi makhluk setengah binatang.
claims.quote: nas noites de lua cheia de sexta-feira e/ou terça-feira, o indivíduo se transformava em uma criatura com metade das característica

description.en: Lutzelfrau (German: [ˈlʊtsl̩ˌfʁaʊ]) or Lutscherl in Eastern Austria, Luz, Luzi, or Luzel in the Bavarian forest, is a witch in German folklore who gives gifts — particularly apples, nuts and dried plums — to children on Saint Lucy's Day (December 13), but also has a "dark Lucia" side (dunkle Luz in Bavaria, and among the German populace (as dunkle Luzia) in outlying neighboring countries. This dark, or malevolent Lutzelfrau is reputed to may disembowel (or drown) naughty children and reward the well-behaved ones with rewards of fruit.

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau, or Lutscherl in eastern Austria and Luz, Luzi or Luzel in the Bavarian Forest, is a witch of German folklore giving apples, nuts and dried plums to children on Saint Lucy's Day (13 December), but with a 'dark Lucia' side said to disembowel or drown naughty children.
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau, atau Lutscherl di Austria timur dan Luz, Luzi, atau Luzel di Hutan Bayern, adalah penyihir cerita rakyat Jerman yang memberi apel, kacang, dan prem kering kepada anak-anak pada Hari Santa Lusia (13 Desember), tetapi juga punya sisi "Lusia gelap" yang konon membelah perut atau menenggelamkan anak nakal.
claims.quote: or Lutscherl in Eastern Austria, Luz , Luzi , or Luzel in the Bavarian forest, is a witch in German folklore who gives gifts — particularly apples, nuts and dried plums — to children on Saint Lucy's Day (December 13), but also has a "dark Lucia" side ... This dark, or malevolent Lutzelfrau is reputed to may disembowel (or drown) naughty children

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau is the standard generic name of the tradition in the Alpine areas of Austria and Bavaria, Germany; in parts of Austria she is simply Lucia, and around Burgenland Luzia, Lutzl or Fersenlutzl.
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau adalah nama umum tradisi ini di wilayah Alpen Austria dan Bayern, Jerman; di sebagian Austria ia disebut Lucia, dan di sekitar Burgenland Luzia, Lutzl, atau Fersenlutzl.
claims.quote: While Lutzefrau serves as one standardized generic name for the tradition in the Alpine areas of Austria and Bavaria, Germany, in parts of Austria, she is more simply called Lucia . Around Burgenland, she is known as Luzia , Lutzl , or Fersenlutzl .

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau is of course associated with Saint Lucy of Syracuse, and Lucia is a name meaning 'luminous'.
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau tentu dikaitkan dengan Santa Lusia dari Sirakusa, dan Lucia adalah nama yang berarti "yang bercahaya".
claims.quote: Lutzelfrau is of course associated with Sankt Lucia (Saint Lucy of Syracuse) and Lucia is a name signifying "luminous" (German: leuchtende ).

claims.statement: In Czechia she is Lucie or Louce, in Slovakia Lucka; Lutzelfrau customs are also common in Slovenia and Croatia, where a 'dark Luz' was contrasted with the Christian saint, and in Slovene she is Lucija.
claims.statement_id: Di Ceko ia dikenal sebagai Lucie atau Louce, di Slowakia Lucka; adat Lutzelfrau juga umum di Slovenia dan Kroasia, tempat "Luz gelap" dikontraskan dengan santa Kristen, dan dalam bahasa Slovenia ia disebut Lucija.
claims.quote: In Czechia, she is known as Lucie or Louce , etc. In Slovakia, she is called Lucka . Lutzelfrau customs are also common in Slovenia and Croatia, where a "dark Luz" was contrasted to the Christian saint. In Slovene, she is called Lucija .

claims.statement: In Burgenland the Lutzelfrau or Pudlfrau visits children on St Lucy's day and 'tosses' sweets through the doorway.
claims.statement_id: Di Burgenland, Lutzelfrau atau Pudlfrau mengunjungi anak-anak pada hari Santa Lusia dan "menggulirkan" manisan lewat ambang pintu.
claims.quote: In Burgenland, Lutzelfrau or Pudlfrau visits the children on St. Lucia's day and "tosses (pudelt ) sweets through the doorway.

claims.statement: Lutzelfrau is a witch of German folklore said to fly at night on her broom, who gives apples, nuts and dried plums to children on Saint Lucy's day (13 December).
claims.statement_id: Lutzelfrau adalah penyihir cerita rakyat Jerman yang konon terbang di malam hari dengan sapunya dan memberi apel, kacang, dan prem kering kepada anak-anak pada hari raya Santa Lusia (13 Desember).
claims.quote: Lutzelfrau est une sorcière du folklore allemand qui volerait la nuit sur son balai, elle offre des cadeaux - en particulier des pommes, des noix et des prunes séchées - aux enfants le jour de la fête de Sainte-Lucie ( 13 décembre ).

claims.statement: According to a mid-19th-century source the Lucia of Bohemia and Tyrol appeared as a goat draped in a bedsheet with horns poking out, paralleled in Scandinavia.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber pertengahan abad ke-19, Lusia di Bohemia dan Tirol tampil sebagai kambing yang berselubung seprai dengan tanduk mencuat, dan hal serupa ada di Skandinavia.
claims.quote: According to a mid-19th century source, the Lucia of Bohemia and Tyrol appeared as a goat, draped in a bedsheet with horns protruding out of the sheet. This is paralleled in Scandinavia.

description.en: Maa-alused are, in Estonian folk religion, mysterious elf-like creatures which live beneath the ground. They were believed to have a parallel existence to that of humans, the principal differences being that all orientations are reversed, such that up becomes down and left becomes right, and that all things possessed by them are diminished in size.

claims.statement: In Estonian folk religion, maa-alused are mysterious elf-like creatures that live beneath the ground.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama rakyat Estonia, maa-alused adalah makhluk misterius mirip peri yang hidup di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Maa-alused are, in Estonian folk religion, mysterious elf-like creatures which live beneath the ground.

claims.statement: They were believed to live a parallel existence to humans, the main differences being that all orientations are reversed, up becoming down and left becoming right, and that everything they own is smaller in size.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dipercaya hidup sejajar dengan manusia, dengan perbedaan utama bahwa semua arah terbalik, atas menjadi bawah dan kiri menjadi kanan, dan semua milik mereka berukuran lebih kecil.
claims.quote: They were believed to have a parallel existence to that of humans, the principal differences being that all orientations are reversed, such that up becomes down and left becomes right, and that all things possessed by them are diminished in size.

claims.statement: The Portuguese article likewise calls maa-alused mysterious elfin creatures of Estonian mythology living under the earth.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Portugis juga menyebut maa-alused sebagai makhluk misterius mirip peri dalam mitologia Estonia yang hidup di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Maa-alused eram, na mitologia estoniana, misteriosas criaturas élficas, as quais viviam sob a terra.

claims.statement: Maa-alused (also maahaldjad) were originally dead beings who later lived under the ground or under the floor.
claims.statement_id: Maa-alused (juga disebut maahaldjad) semula adalah makhluk yang sudah mati, yang kemudian hidup di bawah tanah atau di bawah lantai.
claims.quote: Maa-alused (ka maahaldjad) olid algselt surnud olendid, kes hiljem elasid maa või põranda all.

claims.statement: Maa-alused were known as tiny human-shaped mythical beings mainly in North Estonia (Põhja-Eesti), whose presence was signalled by sounds; they worked as smiths (hammering tiks-tiks) and weavers, appeared above ground as insects or animals (usually frogs), and repaid good deeds generously.
claims.statement_id: Maa-alused dikenal sebagai makhluk mitos kecil berwujud manusia, terutama di Estonia Utara (Põhja-Eesti), yang keberadaannya ditandai suara-suara; mereka bekerja sebagai pandai besi (berbunyi tiks-tiks) dan penenun, muncul di atas tanah sebagai serangga atau hewan (biasanya katak), dan membalas kebaikan dengan murah hati.
claims.quote: Maa-alused olid tuntud pisikeste inimesekujuliste mütoloogiliste olenditena põhiliselt Põhja-Eestis, nende olemasolust andsid märku hääled. Nad tegutsesid seppade (taovad tiks-tiks) ja kangrutena, maa peale ilmusid ka putuka või loomana (harilikult konnana). Neile tehtud heategude eest tasusid rikkalikult.

claims.statement: Angering the maa-alused and maahaldjad (found in South Estonian, Lõuna-Eesti, folk tradition) could bring a disease from the earth, itself also called maa-alused; mainly on Saaremaa, people were not allowed to step on insects or their paths so as not to anger the maa-alused.
claims.statement_id: Membuat marah maa-alused dan maahaldjad (yang muncul dalam tradisi rakyat Estonia Selatan, Lõuna-Eesti) bisa mendatangkan penyakit dari tanah, yang juga disebut maa-alused; terutama di Saaremaa, orang tidak boleh menginjak serangga atau jalur mereka agar maa-alused tidak marah.
claims.quote: Maa-aluste ja maahaldjate (kes esinesid Lõuna-Eesti rahvapärimustes) pahandamine võis kaasa tuua maast saadud haiguse (haigust nimetati samuti maa-alused). Peamiselt Saaremaal ei olnud lubatud putukate peale või nende teeradadele astumine, et mitte pahandada maa-aluseid.

description.id: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (bahasa Thai: แม่นากพระโขนง atau แม่นาคพระโขนง, artinya "Nyonya Nak dari Phra Khanong"), atau kependekannya adalah Mae Nak (bahasa Thai: แม่นาก, "Nyonya Nak") atau Nang Nak (bahasa Thai: นางนาก, "Nona Nak"), adalah sebuah hantu perempuan Thai yang populer dan terkenal. Menurut cerita rakyat lokal, cerita tersebut berdasarkan pada kisah nyata yang terjadi pada awal abad ke-19. Mae Nak memiliki kuilnya sendiri, yang terletak di pinggir kanal Phra Khanong di Bangkok.
description.en: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (Thai: แม่นากพระโขนง, lit. 'Lady Nak of Phra Khanong'), or simply Mae Nak (แม่นาก, 'Lady Nak') or Nang Nak (นางนาก, 'Miss Nak'), is a well-known Thai ghost. According to local folklore the story is based on events that took place during the reign of King Rama IV. A shrine dedicated to Nak was constructed at Wat Mahabut. In 1997, the shrine was relocated to the nearby Suan Luang district of modern Bangkok.

claims.statement: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (แม่นากพระโขนง, 'Lady Nak of Phra Khanong'), or Mae Nak and Nang Nak, is a well-known Thai ghost; folklore says her story is based on events in King Rama IV's reign.
claims.statement_id: Mae Nak Phra Khanong (แม่นากพระโขนง, 'Nyonya Nak dari Phra Khanong'), atau Mae Nak dan Nang Nak, adalah hantu Thailand yang terkenal; menurut cerita rakyat, kisahnya berdasarkan peristiwa pada masa Raja Rama IV.
claims.quote: lit. 'Lady Nak of Phra Khanong'), or simply Mae Nak (แม่นาก, 'Lady Nak') or Nang Nak (นางนาก, 'Miss Nak'), is a well-known Thai ghost. According to local folklore the story is based on events that took place during the reign of King Rama IV.

claims.statement: A shrine to Nak was built at Wat Mahabut and in 1997 relocated to Suan Luang district, Bangkok.
claims.statement_id: Kuil untuk Nak dibangun di Wat Mahabut dan pada 1997 dipindahkan ke distrik Suan Luang, Bangkok.
claims.quote: A shrine dedicated to Nak was constructed at Wat Mahabut. In 1997, the shrine was relocated to the nearby Suan Luang district of modern Bangkok.

claims.statement: While Nak was pregnant, Mak was sent to war and seriously wounded.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Nak hamil, Mak dikirim berperang dan terluka parah.
claims.quote: While Nak was pregnant, Mak was conscripted into the Thai Army and sent to war where he was seriously wounded

claims.statement: Nak stretched her arm to an impossible length to pick up a lime, and Mak realized she was a ghost; he then fled to Wat Mahabut, which ghosts cannot enter.
claims.statement_id: Nak menjulurkan lengannya sangat panjang untuk memungut jeruk nipis dari tanah, dan Mak pun sadar istrinya hantu; ia lalu melarikan diri ke Wat Mahabut yang tak bisa dimasuki hantu.
claims.quote: In her haste to retrieve it, she stretched her arm to an impossible length to pick it up from the ground below. Upon seeing this, Mak realised his wife was a ghost.

claims.statement: Grieving, Nak terrorized Phra Khanong; a powerful monk captured her ghost, sealed it in an earthen jar and threw it into the canal.
claims.statement_id: Nak yang berduka meneror warga Phra Khanong; seorang biksu sakti menangkap arwahnya, mengurungnya dalam guci tanah liat, dan membuangnya ke kanal.
claims.quote: In her grief, Nak terrorised the people of Phra Khanong, furious at them for causing Mak to leave her. However, a powerful monk captured Nak's ghost; and after confining her in an earthen jar, threw it into the Phra Khanong canal.

claims.statement: In another version, the monk assured Nak she would be reunited with her husband in a future life, so she willingly departed.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain, biksu meyakinkan Nak bahwa ia akan bersatu kembali dengan suaminya di kehidupan mendatang, sehingga ia rela pergi ke alam baka.
claims.quote: In another, the monk assured Nak that in a future life she would be reunited with her beloved husband, so she voluntarily departed for the afterlife.

claims.statement: In an 1899 Siam Prabheth article found by historian Anek Nawikamul, K.S.R. Kulap said the story was based on Amdaeng Nak, daughter of a Phra Khanong leader named Khun Si, who died while pregnant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam artikel Siam Prabheth tahun 1899 yang ditemukan sejarawan Anek Nawikamul, K.S.R. Kulap menyebut kisah Mae Nak berdasarkan kehidupan Amdaeng Nak, putri pemimpin Phra Khanong bernama Khun Si, yang meninggal saat hamil.
claims.quote: Kulap claimed the story of Mae Nak was based on the life of Amdaeng Nak (Thai: อำแดงนาก, lit. 'Mrs Nak'), daughter of a Tambon Phra Khanong leader named Khun Si. Amdaeng Nak died while she was pregnant.

claims.statement: Devotees bring offerings with requests, usually women seeking easy childbirth or their husband's exemption from conscription.
claims.statement_id: Para pemuja membawa persembahan disertai permohonan, umumnya perempuan yang meminta persalinan lancar atau agar suaminya bebas dari wajib militer.
claims.quote: Devotees often make offerings, accompanied by a request for help, generally by women seeking easy childbirth or for their husband to be exempted from military conscription.

claims.statement: The legend, believed to date to the early Rattanakosin period, says Mae Nak lived near Wat Mahabut beside a canal.
claims.statement_id: Legenda yang diyakini berasal dari awal periode Rattanakosin ini menyebut Mae Nak tinggal di dekat Wat Mahabut di tepi kanal.
claims.quote: Believed to date back to the early Rattanakosin period (around the 18th century), the legend has it that Mae Nak (“Mae” was used for “Miss” in those days) lived in the area near Wat Mahabut along a canal.

claims.statement: Nak became a pee tai tang klom (ghost of a woman who died in childbirth with the baby inside); out of love her spirit stayed bound to her old life, appearing in human form to do the housework.
claims.statement_id: Nak menjadi pee tai tang klom (arwah perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan dengan bayi masih di kandungan); karena cinta, arwahnya terikat pada kehidupan lamanya dan muncul dalam wujud manusia untuk mengurus rumah.
claims.quote: making her a “Pee tai tang klom” (ghost of a woman who died during childbirth with the baby still inside her). Her body was buried in the cemetery at Wat Mahabut. But because of love, Nak’s spirit was bound to her former life, re-appearing in human form to carry on daily chores at home.

claims.statement: Somdej Toh cremated Nak's body and carved out a piece of her forehead bone to keep as an amulet.
claims.statement_id: Somdej Toh mengkremasi jasad Nak dan mengambil sepotong tulang dahinya untuk disimpan sebagai jimat.
claims.quote: The venerable father then cremated Nak’s body and carved out a piece of her forehead bone to keep as an amulet.

claims.statement: The story also illustrates Buddhist teachings on samsara and the three marks of existence.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini juga menggambarkan ajaran Buddha tentang samsara dan tiga corak keberadaan.
claims.quote: The story also serves as an illustration of Buddhist teachings, namely samsara (the unavoidable cycle of birth, aging, sickness, and death) and the Three Marks of Existence

claims.statement: Prince Damrong recalled asking Wat Phra Kaeo visitors as a child who was most popular, and most answered Mae Nak.
claims.statement_id: Pangeran Damrong bercerita bahwa semasa kecil ia bertanya kepada pengunjung Wat Phra Kaeo siapa orang paling populer, dan kebanyakan menjawab Mae Nak.
claims.quote: Prince Damrong, a son of King Mongkut, revealed that when he was a child, he kept asking Wat Phra Kaeo visitors who was the most popular person in their opinion, and most people answered "Mae Nak".

claims.statement: In Thai folklore ghosts fear sticky Blumea leaves, so Mak hid behind a Blumea balsamifera bush.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Thai, hantu takut daun Blumea yang lengket, sehingga Mak bersembunyi di balik semak Blumea balsamifera.
claims.quote: According to Thai folklore, ghosts are afraid of sticky Blumea leaves so Mak hid behind a Blumea balsamifera

claims.statement: Mae Nak Phra Khanong is a 1959 Thai film directed by Rangsi Thatsanaphayak.
claims.statement_id: Mae Nak Phra Khanong adalah film Thai tahun 1959 karya Rangsi Thatsanaphayak.
claims.quote: Mae Nak Phra Khanong, a 1959 Thai film directed by Rangsi Thatsanaphayak

claims.statement: In other versions, the monk Somdet Phra Phutthachan (To Phrommarangsi) defeats Nak by confining her spirit in her forehead bone, bound to his waistband.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain, biksu Somdet Phra Phutthachan (To Phrommarangsi) mengalahkan Nak dengan mengurung arwahnya dalam tulang dahinya dan mengikatnya di ikat pinggangnya.
claims.quote: In alternative versions, a venerable monk named Somdet Phra Phutthachan (To Phrommarangsi) defeats Nak by confining her spirit in the bone of her forehead and binds it to his waistband.

description.en: Maha Sona or Maha Sohona (Sinhala: මහ සෝණා, මහ සොහොනා) is a devil (or yaksa or dewaya, meaning demon, fiend or monster) in Sinhalese folklore, said to haunt the afterlife. The name Maha Sona denotes "the greatest demon" or "god or demon of the cemetery" in the Sinhala language. He is one of the most feared and commonly known gods or demons in Sri Lanka. According to popular folklore, he was originally a giant who was defeated and decapitated in a duel by another giant, Gotaimbara (who lived in the 1st century BC). His head was then replaced with that of a bear or tiger. He is believed to kill people by crushing their shoulders or by afflicting them with disease. Traditional exorcism rituals are performed to repel the demon in such cases. The Sri Lankan Army's Long Range Reconnaissance Patrol units are popularly known as the "Maha Sohon Brigade", named after this demon.

claims.statement: Maha Sona is a yaksha or demon of Sinhalese folklore in Sri Lanka.
claims.statement_id: Maha Sona adalah yaksa atau iblis dalam cerita rakyat Sinhala di Sri Lanka.
claims.quote: Maha Sona or Maha Sohona (Sinhala: මහ සෝණා, මහ සොහොනා) is a devil (or yaksa or dewaya, meaning demon, fiend or monster)  in Sinhalese folklore, said to haunt the afterlife. The name Maha Sona denotes "the greatest demon" or "god or demon of the cemetery" in the Sinhala language. He is one of the most feared and commonly known gods or demons in Sri Lanka.

claims.statement: His name is interpreted as the greatest demon or god or demon of the cemetery.
claims.statement_id: Namanya ditafsirkan sebagai iblis terbesar atau dewa atau iblis kuburan.
claims.quote: The name Maha Sona denotes "the greatest demon" or "god or demon of the cemetery" in the Sinhala language.

claims.statement: One version identifies his origin as the warrior Ritigala Jayasena, defeated in a duel with Gotaimbara.
claims.statement_id: Satu versi menyebut asalnya sebagai pejuang Ritigala Jayasena yang kalah dalam duel dengan Gotaimbara.
claims.quote: Maha Sona was formerly a human known as Ritigala Jayasena (Jayasena of Ritigala), a fierce warrior who lived during the reign of King Dutugamunu.

claims.statement: In that version a deity attaches a bear's head to revive him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi itu, dewa memasang kepala beruang untuk menghidupkannya kembali.
claims.quote: the deity attaches a bear’s head in its place before reviving him. Due to the urgency, the head is fitted backwards.

claims.statement: Folk songs contain origins not always connecting him with Jayasena.
claims.statement_id: Nyanyian rakyat memuat versi asal-usul yang tidak selalu mengaitkannya dengan Jayasena.
claims.quote: However, folk songs across the country offer alternative origins for Maha Sona, sometimes not linking him to the figure of Jayasena. Depending on the song, he may be depicted as either a demon or a deity. Maha Sona is perhaps the most deeply ingrained supernatural being in the Sri Lankan psyche, unmatched in the fear his name evokes.

claims.statement: He is believed to haunt graveyards, large rocks, hills and three-road junctions.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya menghantui kuburan, batu besar, bukit, dan persimpangan tiga jalan.
claims.quote: Maha Sona is believed to haunt graveyards, searching for human prey. He also haunts large rocks and hills, surrounded by human corpses. Junctions where three roads meet are other haunting grounds of this demon

description.en: The makuragaeshi (枕返し or 反枕, “pillow flip”) is a kind of Japanese spirit or yōkai. They would come at night to one's pillow side and flip over the pillow. They are also considered to change which direction one's head or feet are facing. They are often found in many actual stories from the Edo Period to the modern period, and they are often said to appear as a small child or a bōzu, but there are no clear-cut accounts of how they look. In the Edo Period collection of yōkai pictures, the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō, they are depicted as a miniature Niō.

claims.statement: Makuragaeshi is a Japanese spirit or yōkai.
claims.statement_id: Makuragaeshi adalah roh atau yōkai Jepang.
claims.quote: The makuragaeshi (枕返し or 反枕, “pillow flip”) is a kind of Japanese spirit or yōkai.

claims.statement: It is said to turn over a sleeper’s pillow at night.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon membalik bantal orang yang tidur pada malam hari.
claims.quote: They would come at night to one's pillow side and flip over the pillow.

claims.statement: Other accounts have it reverse the position of a sleeper’s head and feet.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menyebutnya menukar posisi kepala dan kaki orang yang tidur.
claims.quote: They are also considered to change which direction one's head or feet are facing.

claims.statement: Its appearance varies, sometimes resembling a child or monk.
claims.statement_id: Penampilannya beragam, kadang menyerupai anak atau biksu.
claims.quote: They are often found in many actual stories from the Edo Period to the modern period, and they are often said to appear as a small child or a bōzu, but there are no clear-cut accounts of how they look.

claims.statement: An Edo-period illustration depicts a miniature Niō guardian.
claims.statement_id: Ilustrasi zaman Edo menggambarkannya sebagai penjaga Niō kecil.
claims.quote: In the Edo Period collection of yōkai pictures, the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō, they are depicted as a miniature Niō.

claims.statement: An origin story makes it the ghost of someone who died in the room.
claims.statement_id: Satu cerita asal menjadikannya hantu seseorang yang meninggal di kamar itu.
claims.quote: Most often they linked to the ghosts of people — particularly children — who died in the room they come to haunt.

description.en: The Manaia is a mythological creature in Māori culture, and is a common motif in Māori carving and jewellery. The Manaia is usually depicted as having the head of a bird and the tail of a fish and the body of a man, though it is sometimes depicted as a bird, a serpent, or a human figure in profile. Other interpretations include a seahorse and a lizard. The word manaia is cognate with the founding Samoan term fa'amanaia, and relevant to the Niuean fakamanaia, both meaning to make a decoration or embellishment. The Manaia is traditionally believed to be the messenger between the earthly world of mortals and the domain of the spirits, and its symbol is used as a guardian against evil. In this form, it is usually represented in a figure-of-eight shape, the upper half culminating in a bird-like beak. This form was also widely used in designs of door and window lintels and other architectural features, as well as in ceremonial hafts of weapons. A study of Māori carving suggests that every naturalistic figure there is an equivalent Manaia form which can be seen as a distorted profile-face version of the equivalent full-face figure. It may be that the Manaia represents some spiritual or inner facet of the full face figure. Related Manaia-like symbols are also found in other Polynesian cultures, such as in Hawaii and Easter Island. The manaia is a useful motif in carving, as it can be distorted to fit any shape and blended into many different designs. As such, it can be used to fill the empty spaces in wood carving, and in many compositions the background between the main figures is filled in with Manaia. It is a very common form in Maori jewellery (possibly only less common than the hei-tiki and hei matau), and is often found worn as a pendant carved from bone or greenstone. Manaia designs vary subtly in form between iwi, though they are often depicted as three-fingered, with these digits representing the trinity of birth, life, and death. A fourth finger, representing the circular rhythms of the life cycle and the afterlife, is also sometimes shown.

claims.statement: The Manaia is a mythological creature in Māori culture, common in carving and jewellery.
claims.statement_id: Manaia adalah makhluk mitologi dalam budaya Māori dan motif umum dalam ukiran serta perhiasan.
claims.quote: The Manaia is a mythological creature in Māori culture, and is a common motif in Māori carving and jewellery.

claims.statement: The Manaia is usually depicted with bird head, fish tail, and human body.
claims.statement_id: Manaia biasanya digambarkan berkepala burung, berekor ikan, dan bertubuh manusia.
claims.quote: The Manaia is usually depicted as having the head of a bird and the tail of a fish and the body of a man, though it is sometimes depicted as a bird, a serpent, or a human figure in profile.

claims.statement: The Manaia is believed to be the messenger between mortals and spirits, and a guardian against evil.
claims.statement_id: Manaia dipercaya sebagai utusan antara dunia fana dan alam roh, serta simbol pelindung dari kejahatan.
claims.quote: The Manaia is traditionally believed to be the messenger between the earthly world of mortals and the domain of the spirits, and its symbol is used as a guardian against evil.

claims.statement: In this form it is represented in a figure-of-eight shape culminating in a bird-like beak.
claims.statement_id: Dalam wujud ini ia biasa digambarkan berbentuk angka delapan dengan paruh burung di bagian atasnya.
claims.quote: In this form, it is usually represented in a figure-of-eight shape, the upper half culminating in a bird-like beak.

claims.statement: Related Manaia-like symbols are found in other Polynesian cultures such as Hawaii.
claims.statement_id: Simbol serupa Manaia juga ditemukan dalam kebudayaan Polynesian lainnya seperti di Hawaii.
claims.quote: Related Manaia-like symbols are also found in other Polynesian cultures, such as in Hawaii and Easter Island.

claims.statement: Manaia designs are often depicted three-fingered representing birth, life, and death.
claims.statement_id: Desain Manaia sering berjarikan tiga yang melambangkan trinitas kelahiran, kehidupan, dan kematian.
claims.quote: Manaia designs vary subtly in form between iwi, though they are often depicted as three-fingered, with these digits representing the trinity of birth, life, and death.

description.en: In Indian folklore, the Mande Burung is an alleged ape-like creature said to inhabit the Meghalaya subtropical forests in the remote Garo Hills of the Northeast India. Generally described as a large, hairy bipedal hominoid, some believe that this animal, or its relatives, may be found around the world under different regional names, such as the Yeti of Tibet and Nepal, the Ban-manush in Bangladesh, the Yeren of mainland China, and the Bigfoot of the Pacific northwest region of the United States and all of the Canadian provinces, including British Columbia where the majority of all Sasquatch reports and sightings occur.

claims.statement: Mande Barung is an alleged apelike creature said to inhabit Meghalaya forests in the Garo Hills.
claims.statement_id: Mande Barung adalah makhluk mirip kera yang dikabarkan menghuni hutan Meghalaya di Perbukitan Garo.
claims.quote: In Indian folklore, the Mande Burung is an alleged ape-like creature said to inhabit the Meghalaya subtropical forests in the remote Garo Hills of the Northeast India.

claims.statement: It is generally described as a large, hairy, bipedal hominoid.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai humanoid besar, berbulu, dan berjalan dengan dua kaki.
claims.quote: Generally described as a large, hairy bipedal hominoid

description.en: In Canadian folklore, the Manipogo is a lake monster said to live in Lake Manitoba, Manitoba, Canada. The creature was dubbed Manipogo in 1960, the name echoing British Columbia's Ogopogo. It is the namesake of the Manipogo Provincial Park. There is also a monster called Winnepogo, named for either Lake Winnipegosis or Lake Winnipeg, thought possibly to be the same creature since the lakes are connected. The community of St. Laurent on the southeast shore of Lake Manitoba holds a yearly Manipogo Festival during the first week of March.

claims.statement: In Canadian folklore, Manipogo is a lake monster said to live in Lake Manitoba, Canada.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kanada, Manipogo adalah monster danau yang konon hidup di Danau Manitoba, Kanada.
claims.quote: In Canadian folklore, the Manipogo is a lake monster said to live in Lake Manitoba, Manitoba, Canada.

claims.statement: The creature was named Manipogo in 1960, echoing British Columbia's Ogopogo.
claims.statement_id: Nama Manipogo diberikan pada 1960 dengan meniru nama Ogopogo dari British Columbia.
claims.quote: The creature was dubbed Manipogo in 1960, the name echoing British Columbia's Ogopogo.

claims.statement: Manipogo Provincial Park is named after it.
claims.statement_id: Taman Provinsi Manipogo dinamai menurut makhluk ini.
claims.quote: It is the namesake of the Manipogo Provincial Park.

claims.statement: The community of St. Laurent on Lake Manitoba's southeast shore holds a Manipogo Festival every first week of March.
claims.statement_id: Komunitas St. Laurent di tepi tenggara Danau Manitoba mengadakan Festival Manipogo setiap minggu pertama bulan Maret.
claims.quote: The community of St. Laurent on the southeast shore of Lake Manitoba holds a yearly Manipogo Festival during the first week of March.

claims.statement: It is described as having a brownish-black body with at least one hump showing above the water.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan bertubuh cokelat kehitaman dengan sedikitnya satu punuk yang tampak di atas air.
claims.quote: It is described as having "a brownish-black body and at least one hump that shows above the water."

claims.statement: Its head is likened to a horse's, camel's or sheep's, while others say it is flat and diamond-shaped.
claims.statement_id: Kepalanya kadang disamakan dengan kepala kuda, unta, atau domba; ada pula yang menyebutnya pipih dan berbentuk belah ketupat.
claims.quote: Its head is sometimes compared to that of a horse, camel, or sheep, while others have claimed it was flat and diamond-shaped.

claims.statement: It reportedly shrieks or cries as it surfaces.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon mengeluarkan jeritan saat muncul ke permukaan.
claims.quote: It is purported to let out a shriek or cry as it surfaces

claims.statement: Local First Nations people have legends of serpent-like creatures in Lake Manitoba going back hundreds of years.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk First Nations setempat punya legenda tentang makhluk mirip ular di Danau Manitoba sejak ratusan tahun lalu.
claims.quote: The local First Nations population has legends of serpent-like creatures in Lake Manitoba going back hundreds of years.

claims.statement: The first documented sighting by a white settler was in September 1909, when Hudson's Bay Company fur trader Valentine McKay claimed to see a huge creature.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan pertama yang terdokumentasi oleh pemukim kulit putih terjadi pada September 1909, ketika pedagang bulu Valentine McKay dari Hudson's Bay Company mengaku melihat makhluk besar.
claims.quote: The first documented sighting by a white settler came in September 1909, when Hudson's Bay Company fur trader Valentine McKay claimed to see a huge creature in Cedar Lake near Graves Point on Lake Manitoba.

claims.statement: Some sceptics think the monster is a swimming moose with its head and humped back showing.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian skeptis menduga monster itu sebenarnya rusa moose yang berenang dengan kepala dan punggung bungkuknya terlihat.
claims.quote: Other sceptics believe that the so-called monster is actually a swimming moose with its head above the surface and its humped back showing as well.

claims.statement: In 1936 fisherman Oscar Fredrickson found an animal skull in his fishing net.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1936 nelayan Oscar Fredrickson menemukan sebuah tengkorak hewan di jaring ikannya.
claims.quote: 1936年：渔民奥斯卡·弗雷德里克森（Oscar Fredrickson）在拉起一网鱼的时候，发现在网里捞起了一块动物的头盖骨。

claims.statement: Soon after, Fredrickson's house burned down for unknown reasons and the skull was lost.
claims.statement_id: Tak lama kemudian rumah Fredrickson terbakar tanpa sebab yang jelas, dan tengkorak itu hilang.
claims.quote: 但不久后弗雷德里克森家发生不明原因的火灾，把整个家都烧毁了，而那块从马尼托巴湖捞起的头盖骨也下落不明。

claims.statement: Local indigenous people also have legends of a water monster; according to this source, the creature was named Manipogo in 1957, echoing British Columbia's Ogopogo.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk asli setempat juga punya legenda monster air; menurut sumber ini, makhluk itu dinamai Manipogo pada 1957 dengan meniru Ogopogo dari British Columbia.
claims.quote: 当地的土著居民也有水怪的传说。这种生物在1957年被命名为马尼波戈，以响应不列颠哥伦比亚省发现的欧戈波戈。

description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Brasil, mapinguari atau mapinguary, juga disebut juma, adalah makhluk mengerikan yang dikatakan hidup di hutan hujan Amazon. Penggambaran mapinguari bervariasi. Kadang-kadang digambarkan sebagai cyclop humanoid berbulu. Beberapa orang mengklaim bahwa mahkluk itu mirip sloth tanah raksasa, hewan yang telah lama punah yang dikatakan mirip. Monster ini sering dikisahkan memiliki mulut menganga di perutnya.
description.en: The Mapinguari or Mapinguary is a cryptid from Brazilian folklore. The Mapinguari is often described as an extremely foul-smelling, hairy animal that is distinct from the North American Bigfoot. Descriptions further allege that the cryptid is a man-eating creature with hook-shaped nails, backwards-facing feet, a bipedal gait, a gaping mouth in its abdomen, and a single eye like the mythological Cyclops.

claims.statement: The Mapinguari is often described as an extremely foul-smelling, hairy animal that is distinct from the North American Bigfoot.
claims.statement_id: Mapinguari kerap digambarkan sebagai hewan berbulu yang amat berbau busuk.
claims.quote: The Mapinguari is often described as an extremely foul-smelling, hairy animal that is distinct from the North American Bigfoot.

claims.statement: Descriptions further allege that the cryptid is a man-eating creature with hook-shaped nails, backwards-facing feet, a bipedal gait, a gaping mouth in its abdomen, and a single eye like the mythological Cyclops.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini digambarkan memangsa manusia dengan kuku kait, kaki terbalik, dan mulut menganga di perut.
claims.quote: Descriptions further allege that the cryptid is a man-eating creature with hook-shaped nails, backwards-facing feet, a bipedal gait, a gaping mouth in its abdomen, and a single eye like the mythological Cyclops.

claims.statement: The creature's size has been depicted as either comparable to a human, or larger.
claims.statement_id: Ukuran tubuh makhluk ini digambarkan seukuran manusia atau lebih besar.
claims.quote: The creature's size has been depicted as either comparable to a human, or larger.

claims.statement: The other recurring feature of the Mapinguari is a large, single eye in either the abdomen or the forehead, like a Cyclops.
claims.statement_id: Ciri berulang lainnya adalah mata tunggal besar di perut atau dahi mirip Cyclops.
claims.quote: The other recurring feature of the Mapinguari is a large, single eye in either the abdomen or the forehead, like a Cyclops.

description.en: In Scandinavian folklore, a marmennill (pronounced /mɑɹ'mɛnɪtlᵊ/) (also marmandill, marbendill, or margmelli) is a merman that often features in stories after having been accidentally caught at sea by fishermen. The creature is typically known for its ability to see the future or to reveal otherwise hidden knowledge, often laughing when he sees others acting foolishly.

claims.statement: In Scandinavian folklore the marmennill is a merman often featured after being accidentally caught by fishermen; he is known for seeing the future or revealing hidden knowledge, and often laughs at others' folly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia (Scandinavian), marmennill adalah manusia laut yang sering muncul dalam kisah setelah tak sengaja tertangkap nelayan; ia dikenal dapat melihat masa depan atau mengungkap pengetahuan tersembunyi dan sering tertawa melihat orang bertindak bodoh.
claims.quote: is a merman that often features in stories after having been accidentally caught at sea by fishermen. The creature is typically known for its ability to see the future or to reveal otherwise hidden knowledge, often laughing when he sees others acting foolishly.

claims.statement: Marmennill is rendered 'merman', 'sea-mannikin' or 'sea-goblin'; Hauksbók's Landnámabók spells it margmelli, another medieval variant is marmandill, and the modern Icelandic form is marbendill.
claims.statement_id: Marmennill diterjemahkan "manusia laut", "manusia kecil laut", atau "goblin laut"; dalam Landnámabók versi Hauksbók dieja margmelli, varian abad pertengahan lain marmandill, dan bentuk Islandia (Icelandic) modernnya marbendill.
claims.quote: Marmennill has been variously translated as "merman", "mereman", "sea-mannikin" and "sea-goblin". In the Hauksbók version of Landnámabók, it is spelt as margmelli , with other medieval variants including marmandill . The modern Icelandic form is marbendill .

claims.statement: In Landnámabók Grímr (Grim) hauled up a merman and asked their fortune and where to settle in Iceland; it said there was no need to foretell Grímr's fortune, but the boy's in the sealskin bag, who would settle where the mare Skálm (Skalm) lay down under her load.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Landnámabók, Grímr (Grim) menarik naik manusia laut dan bertanya nasib mereka dan di mana menetap di Islandia (Iceland); jawabnya, tak perlu meramal nasib Grímr, melainkan anak dalam kantong kulit anjing laut, yang akan menetap di tempat kuda betina Skálm (Skalm) rebah di bawah muatannya.
claims.quote: Grim drew up a mereman and when he came up asked him "What do you foretell shall be our fortune, or where shall we settle in Iceland ? The mereman answered, "No need to tell the fortune of you and your men, but rather of the lad that lays in the seal bag, he shall there settle and take land where Skalm your mare lays down under her load,"

claims.statement: Later that winter Grímr (Grim) and his men rowed out while the boy was ashore, and the whole crew was lost; another prophetic marmennill appears in the 14th-century Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian di musim dingin Grímr (Grim) dan anak buahnya melaut sementara anak itu di darat, lalu seluruh awak hilang; marmennill peramal lain muncul dalam Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka abad ke-14.
claims.quote: Later in the winter Grim and his men rowed out, but the lad was upon land; then the whole crew was lost. Another prophetic marmennill appears in the 14th-century Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka.

claims.statement: The tale 'Þá hló marbendill' tells of a farmer who catches a marbendill at sea and takes it home; on the way it laughs at him three times.
claims.statement_id: Kisah "Þá hló marbendill" menceritakan petani yang menangkap marbendill di laut dan membawanya pulang; dalam perjalanan makhluk itu menertawakannya tiga kali.
claims.quote: It tells the story of a farmer who catches a marbendill out at sea and takes it home with him. On the way home, the creature laughs three times at the farmer.

claims.statement: In Icelandic (isländsk) folk belief the marmennill is a sea being which, like a mermaid, has a human upper body and a fish tail; it was thought able to foretell the future; its female counterpart was Margygur, and the corresponding being in Sweden (Sverige) and Denmark (Danmark) was Havmannen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Islandia (isländsk), marmennill adalah makhluk laut yang, seperti putri duyung, bertubuh atas manusia dan berekor ikan; ia dianggap mampu meramal masa depan; padanan perempuannya Margygur, dan makhluk padanannya di Swedia (Sverige) dan Denmark (Danmark) disebut Havmannen.
claims.quote: Marmennill är i isländsk folktro ett havsväsen som liksom sjöjungfrun har en människas överkropp och en fiskstjärt som underkropp. Varelsen menades ha förmågan att förutspå framtiden. Den kvinnliga motsvarigheten kallades Margygur och en motsvarande varelse i Sverige och Danmark kallades Havmannen.

claims.statement: The phrase þá hló marbendill ('then the merman laughed') is used in Iceland for a sudden spiteful laugh, after the folktale motif.
claims.statement_id: Ungkapan þá hló marbendill ("lalu manusia laut itu tertawa") dipakai di Islandia (Iceland) untuk tawa mendadak yang dengki, merujuk motif dalam kisah rakyat.
claims.quote: The phrase þá hló marbendill ("then the merman laughed") is used in Iceland to refer to a sudden and spiteful fit of laughter in reference to the motif in folktales.

claims.statement: In exchange for freedom the creature reveals he laughed because the farmer's wife is unfaithful, his dog truly loves him, and the tuft of grass hides a treasure.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai tebusan kebebasannya, makhluk itu mengungkap bahwa ia tertawa karena istri petani tak setia, anjingnya sungguh menyayanginya, dan gundukan rumput itu menyembunyikan harta.
claims.quote: In exchange for his freedom, the creature reveals that he laughed at the farmer because his wife is unfaithful, his dog truly loves him, and the tuft of grass conceals a treasure.

claims.statement: Once returned to the sea, however, he utters several prophecies in verse.
claims.statement_id: Namun setelah dikembalikan ke laut, ia menyampaikan beberapa nubuat dalam bentuk syair.
claims.quote: Upon being returned to the sea, however, he issues several prophecies in poetic verse.

description.en: A Matagot is a spirit in French folklore that tends to take the form of a black cat. The name "Matagot" comes from the Spanish mater (to kill) and gothos (goths).

claims.statement: A matagot is a spirit of French folklore that usually takes the form of a black cat.
claims.statement_id: Matagot adalah roh dalam cerita rakyat Prancis yang biasanya berwujud kucing hitam.
claims.quote: A Matagot is a spirit in French folklore that tends to take the form of a black cat.

claims.statement: Matagots are generally evil, but some help, like the 'magician cat' that brings wealth to a home if well fed.
claims.statement_id: Matagot umumnya jahat, tetapi sebagian dapat membantu, seperti "kucing penyihir" yang membawa kekayaan ke rumah bila diberi makan dengan baik.
claims.quote: Matagots are generally evil, but some may prove helpful, like the "magician cat" said to bring wealth into a home if it is well fed.

claims.statement: A wealth-bringing matagot must be lured with a fresh plump chicken and carried home without its new owner looking back.
claims.statement_id: Matagot pembawa kekayaan harus dipancing dengan ayam segar yang gemuk, lalu dibawa pulang tanpa pemiliknya menoleh ke belakang.
claims.quote: Traditionally, a wealth-bringing matagot must be lured with a fresh, plump chicken, then carried home by its new owner without the human looking back.

claims.statement: If the cat gets the first mouthful of food and drink at every meal and is well treated, it brings good luck; a matagot can serve up to nine masters at once.
claims.statement_id: Bila kucing itu diberi suapan pertama makanan dan minuman setiap kali makan dan dirawat baik, ia membawa keberuntungan; matagot konon dapat melayani sampai sembilan tuan sekaligus.
claims.quote: If the cat is given the first mouthful of food and drink at every meal and otherwise treated well, it will bring the human good fortune. A matagot is said to be able to serve up to nine masters at once.

claims.statement: In Gascon tradition one must not keep the matagot for life: a dying owner suffers a long agony until he frees it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi Gascogne, matagot tidak boleh dipelihara seumur hidup: pemilik yang sekarat akan lama menderita selama belum membebaskannya.
claims.quote: In Gascony traditions, you must not keep the matagot all your life: if the owner is dying, they will suffer a long agony, as long as they don't free the matagot.

claims.statement: In Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald the matagot is a hairless black cat-like creature that can multiply at will.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald, matagot adalah makhluk mirip kucing hitam tak berbulu yang dapat menggandakan diri.
claims.quote: In Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald the matagot is a hairless, black, cat-like creature with the ability to multiply at will.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the chat d'argent, mandragot or matagot of Breton, Gascon, Provençal and Languedoc folklore is a usually black, diabolical cat a sorcerer obtains in exchange for his soul.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, chat d'argent, mandragot, atau matagot dalam cerita rakyat Bretagne, Gascogne, Provence, dan Languedoc adalah kucing setan, biasanya hitam, yang diperoleh penyihir dengan menukar jiwanya.
claims.quote: Le chat d'argent, mandragot ou matagot est, dans le folklore de Bretagne, de Gascogne, de Provence, et du Languedoc, un chat généralement noir et diabolique obtenu par un sorcier en échange de son âme.

claims.statement: It roams mysterious places at night and returns at dawn with gold louis for its master; if neglected or unrewarded it takes offence and may take cruel revenge.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkeliaran di tempat misterius pada malam hari dan pulang saat fajar membawa koin emas louis untuk tuannya; bila diabaikan atau tidak diberi imbalan, ia tersinggung dan dapat membalas dengan kejam.
claims.quote: Il est censé se promener dans quelques lieux mystérieux pendant la nuit, et revenir à l'aube avec un stock de louis d'or pour son maître. Si celui-ci le néglige ou ne le récompense pas, le chat s'offense et peut se venger cruellement.

claims.statement: Sometimes the cat serves nine masters and leads the last to hell.
claims.statement_id: Kadang kucing ini melayani sembilan tuan dan membawa tuan terakhir ke neraka.
claims.quote: Parfois, ce chat serait censé servir non pas un, mais neuf maîtres, et conduire le dernier en enfer.

claims.statement: The Catalan article calls the matagot, also mantagot, a spirit of Occitan mythology known especially in Provence and Languedoc.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Katalan menyebut matagot, juga mantagot, roh mitologi Occitania yang terutama dikenal di Provence dan Languedoc.
claims.quote: El matagot (en occità: lo matagòt), anomenat també mantagot (mantagòt), és un geni propi de la mitologia d'Occitània, conegut sobretot a la Provença i el Llenguadoc.

description.en: The mazapégul, also known by several other names in Romagnol, are mischievous nocturnal elves in the folklore of Romagna, especially around the Apennines of Forlì, in northern Italy. Portrayed as homunculi with feline features, mazapégul wear a distinctive red cap, which they require to perform their mischief. They disrupt sleep, make objects disappear, and disturb animals, especially horses, whose tails and manes they braid. Mazapégul are particularly attracted to beautiful young girls, with whom they tend to sleep and compliment. A mazapégul's power can be removed by stealing its cap, performing an action to disgust the elf, or reciting a poem while walking along a rope. The mazapégul, particularly its red cap, features in Romagnol carnival costumes. It is often incorporated into cultural events in Romagna aimed at children and families, and its name has been adopted in music and by a brewery.

claims.statement: The mazapégul, known by several other Romagnol names, are mischievous night elves of the folklore of Romagna, especially around the Apennines of Forlì in northern Italy.
claims.statement_id: Mazapégul, yang punya banyak nama lain dalam bahasa Romagnol, adalah peri malam yang usil dalam cerita rakyat Romagna, terutama di Pegunungan Apennine sekitar Forlì, Italia utara.
claims.quote: The mazapégul, also known by several other names in Romagnol, are mischievous nocturnal elves in the folklore of Romagna, especially around the Apennines of Forlì, in northern Italy.

claims.statement: They are shown as a cross between apes and homunculi with grey fur, also like cats or monkeys, wearing a distinctive red cap they need for their mischief.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai campuran kera dan manusia kecil berbulu kelabu, mirip kucing atau monyet, dan memakai topi merah khas yang mereka perlukan untuk berbuat usil.
claims.quote: The elves are portrayed as a cross between apes and homunculi, with grey fur, also resembling cats or monkeys. They wear a distinctive red cap, which they require to perform their mischief.

claims.statement: The mazapégul are blamed for nightmares, including sleep paralysis and choking sensations, tousling sleeping women's hair, stomach aches, vanishing objects, clashing cymbals and flying dishes.
claims.statement_id: Mazapégul dianggap menyebabkan mimpi buruk, termasuk kelumpuhan tidur dan rasa tercekik, mengacak rambut perempuan yang tidur, sakit perut, menghilangkan benda, memainkan simbal, dan membuat piring beterbangan.
claims.quote: The mazapégul are credited for causing nightmares, including sleep paralysis or sensations of suffocation, ruffling women's hair in their sleep, causing stomach pains, making objects disappear, playing the cymbals, causing dishes to fly, and making victims gain weight.

claims.statement: In the countryside they bother animals, especially horses, which wake sweating with braided tails and manes.
claims.statement_id: Di pedesaan mereka mengganggu hewan, terutama kuda, yang bangun pagi dengan tubuh berkeringat serta ekor dan surai terkepang.
claims.quote: In the countryside, they disturb animals, especially horses, who wake in the mornings covered in sweat and with braided tails and manes.

claims.statement: Drawn to pretty girls, they enter their rooms at night, fall asleep on their stomachs and praise them: 'What beautiful eyes! What beautiful hair!'
claims.statement_id: Tertarik pada gadis cantik, mereka masuk ke kamar gadis pada malam hari, tidur di atas perutnya, dan memujinya: "Betapa indah matamu! Betapa indah rambutmu!"
claims.quote: Attracted by beautiful young girls, the elves enter their rooms at night and fall asleep on their stomachs. They compliment them, saying: "What beautiful eyes! What beautiful hair!"

claims.statement: If its cap is stolen or thrown down the well, the thief may be pestered at night with the cry 'give me back my cap!'
claims.statement_id: Bila topinya dicuri atau dilempar ke sumur, si pencuri bisa diganggu setiap malam dengan tuntutan "kembalikan topiku!".
claims.quote: If its cap is stolen or thrown into the well, either its vanquisher is tormented at night with the demand of "give me back my cap!"

claims.statement: Grains of rice scattered on a windowsill keep the mazapégul busy counting them until daybreak.
claims.statement_id: Menaburkan butir beras di ambang jendela membuat mazapégul sibuk menghitungnya sampai fajar.
claims.quote: sprinkling grains of rice on a windowsill so that the mazapégul is distracted by counting them until daybreak.

claims.statement: The mazapégul descend from the incubus, a demon that troubled sleepers and preyed on women, and share traits with elves elsewhere, such as the Laurieddhu of southern Italy and those of the French Vosges.
