description.en: The Witches of Anaga were (according to popular belief) women who were devoted to covens in the mountainous area of Anaga in the northeast of the island of Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain). These rituals were held in an area in the mountains of Anaga in the dorsal between San Andrés and Taganana. The area is called "El Bailadero", which refers to the dances performed by witches around a bonfire. It was believed that after the covens, witches came down to the coast to swim naked. With the passage of time, due to the influence of vampire stories in Eastern Europe, this led to the myth that witches incorporated the aspect of drinking blood, thus making them witch-vampires; typically tales were created that these witches sucked the blood of newborns as they slept in their cribs. There is also a theory that the origin of this legend was from pagan rituals associated with rituals that celebrated guanches rain; these rituals were considered as an act of witchcraft by the Catholic Church.

description.en: The Linton Worm is a mythical beast referred to in a Scottish Borders legend dating back to the 12th century. "Wyrm" is the Old English for serpent. A 12th-century writer believed it to be "In length three Scots yards and bigger than an ordinary man’s leg – in form and callour to our common muir edders." The myth is similar to that of the Lambton Worm.

claims.quote: The monster lived in a hollow on the northeast side of Linton Hill, a spot still known as the "Worm’s Den", at Linton in Roxburghshire on the Scottish borders. Emerging from its lair at dusk and dawn to ravage the countryside, eating crops, livestock and people, it proved invulnerable to the weapons ranged against it.

claims.statement: The news reached John de Somerville, the reckless Laird of Lariston.

claims.statement: As at a joust, De Somerville plunged his burning lance into the monster's mouth and throat, mortally wounding it.

claims.quote: As if at a joust he attacked it, plunging his burning lance into the monster's gaping mouth and down its throat, mortally wounding it.

claims.statement: The Linton Worm's death throes shaped the hills (wormington); its tail brought the mountain down, burying it.

claims.statement: Folklorist Ernest Marwick notes the Linton worm was slain like the Stoor worm of Orkney, also killed with burning peat.
claims.statement_id: Folklorist Ernest Marwick menyoroti kemiripan cara membunuh Linton worm dengan Stoor worm dari Orkney, yang juga dibunuh dengan gambut menyala.
claims.quote: The Orcadian folklorist Ernest Marwick highlights the similarity between the method used to kill the Linton worm and those recounted in the slaying of the Stoor worm of Orkney, which was also killed with burning peat.

claims.statement: He was made Royal Falconer, knighted and First Barrone of Linton; the Somervilles' crest was a wyvern on a wheel.

description.en: The xana (Asturian: /ˈʃana/or [ˈɕa.na]) is a character found in Asturian mythology. Always female, she is a creature of extraordinary beauty believed to live in fountains, rivers, waterfalls, or forested regions with pure water. The origin of the Asturian word xana is unclear, though some scholars see it as a derivation from the Latin name for the goddess Diana. References to where the mythological xanas lived are still common in Asturian toponyms. They also appear in Eastern Galician and Cantabrian mythology (Anjanas).

claims.quote: The xana (Asturian: /ˈʃana/or [ˈɕa.na]) is a character found in Asturian mythology. Always female, she is a creature of extraordinary beauty believed to live in fountains, rivers, waterfalls, or forested regions with pure water.

description.en: Xiaotian Quan (Chinese: 哮天犬 or 嘯天犬; pinyin: Xiàotiān Quǎn; lit. 'Howling/Barking Celestial Dog') is a Chinese mythological beast and companion of the Chinese god Erlang Shen. Depicted as a black dog, it assists Erlang Shen in battle by using its powerful bite and howl to attack, maul, or subdue demons. Xiaotian Quan appears in Journey to the West, Fengshen Yanyi, and other legends about Erlang Shen, such as Lotus Lantern and several Chinese folktales.

description.id: Pada mitologi Aztek, Xiuhcoatl (ular api) adalah personifikasi dari musim kemarau dan tanah hangus. Xiuhcoatl dihadirkan dalam artefak sebagai ular, dan berhubungan dengan pemujaan api Xiuhtecuhtli. Xiuhcoatl merupakan makhluk dalam mitologi Aztek. Makhluk ini merupakan ular api dengan setengah badan dan moncong yang dibagi-bagi yang bisa membelok dengan tajam ke belakang. Xiuhcoatl juga berhubungan dengan dewa api Meksiko Tengah.
description.en: In Aztec religion, Xiuhcōātl [ʃiʍˈkoːaːt͡ɬ] was a mythological serpent, regarded as the spirit form of Xiuhtecuhtli, the Aztec fire deity sometimes represented as an atlatl or a weapon wielded by Huitzilopochtli. Xiuhcoatl is a Classical Nahuatl word that translates as "turquoise serpent" and also carries the symbolic and descriptive translation of "fire serpent". Xiuhcoatl was a common subject of Aztec art, including illustrations in Aztec codices, and was used as a back ornament on representations of both Xiuhtecuhtli and Huitzilopochtli. Xiuhcoatl is interpreted as the embodiment of the dry season and was the weapon of the sun. Apparently, the royal diadem (or xiuhuitzolli, "pointed turquoise thing") of the Aztec emperors represented the tail of the Xiuhcoatl, the fire serpent.

description.id: Yaksa (Dewanagari: यक्ष; ,IAST: Yakṣa,; Pali: [yakha] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan)) adalah roh-roh alam yang biasanya baik hati tetapi kadang-kadang usilan atau angin-anginan, dan dikait-kaitkan dengan air, kesuburan, pohon, hutan, harta benda, serta alam liar. Yaksa disebut-sebut di dalam kesusastraan agama Hindu, Jaina, dan Buddha, serta dicitrakan di kuil-kuil Asia Selatan dan Asia Tenggara dari abad kuno maupun abad madya sebagai dewa pelindung. Bentuk feminin dari yaksa adalah "yaksi" atau yaksini (Sanskerta: यक्षिणी, yakṣiṇī; Pali: [yakhini] Galat: {{Lang}}: text has italic markup (bantuan)). Penggambarannya di dalam kesusastraan agama Hindu, Jaina, dan Buddha membuat yakṣa terkesan berkepribadian ganda. Yakṣa dapat disifatkan sebagai peri penunggu hutan atau gunung, tetapi dapat pula disifatkan sebagai butakala, dedemit alam liar yang suka menghadang dan memangsa manusia yang kebetulan lewat, mirip dengan rakṣasa.
description.en: The Yakshas (Sanskrit: यक्ष, IAST: Yakṣa, Pali: Yakkha) are a broad class of nature spirits in Hindu mythology which are associated with water, trees, forests, wilderness, treasure, and fertility. They are usually considered benevolent, and sometimes mischievous or capricious. They appear in Hindu, Jain and Buddhist texts, as well as ancient and medieval temples of South Asia and Southeast Asia as guardian deities. The feminine form of the word is IAST: Yakṣī or Yakshini (Sanskrit: यक्षिणी, IAST: Yakṣiṇī; Pali: Yakkhini). In Hindu, Jain and Buddhist texts, the yakṣas have a dual personality. A yakṣa may be an inoffensive nature spirit associated with woods and mountains, or a darker version of the yakṣa which is a kind of Bhoota (ghost) that haunts the wilderness and waylays and devours travellers, similar to the rakṣasas. A unique cultural dance form related to the Yakshas is Yakshagana. Yakshagana is a traditional stage performance, found in Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kasaragod district and Uttara Kannada, Shimoga and western Chikmagalur districts, in the state of Karnataka.

description.id: Yamauba (山姥, nenek gunung) atau dibaca Yamamba adalah wanita tua golongan yōkai yang hidup di tengah hutan di gunung dalam legenda dan cerita rakyat Jepang. Ia digambarkan bertubuh tinggi, rambutnya panjang beruban semua, sudut luar mata tertarik ke atas, dan mulutnya lebar hingga ke telinga. Nama lain untuknya adalah onibaba (鬼婆, nenek oni) dan kijo (鬼女). Menjelma sebagai wanita berparas cantik, yamauba akan menawarkan tempat menginap kepada pelancong atau yang kemalaman di tengah gunung. Orang itu juga akan ditawari makan dan minum. Setelah tertidur, orang itu akan dimakan oleh yamauba. Legenda yamauba diperkirakan berasal dari tradisi membuang nenek di gunung dan cerita rakyat Ubasuteyama.

description.id: Yamawaro atau Yamawarawa (山章) adalah salah satu yokai gunung dalam cerita rakyat Jepang. Menurut cerita, awalnya Yamawaro merupakan dewa gunung yang tinggal di wilayah Kyushu. Yamawaro memiliki dua sifat yang berbeda tergantung dari cara manusia memandangnya. Jika ia dihormati, ia akan membantu masyarakat, sedangkan jika diabaikan ia akan membahayakan desa.
description.en: Yamawaro (山童; or yamawarau) is a yōkai (spirit) said to appear in mountains in Western Japan, starting in the Kyūshū region. According to mythology, it is sometimes said that they are kappa that have come to dwell in the mountains. Yamawaro are known by a number of different, similar terms; in Ashikita District, Kumamoto Prefecture, they are also known as yamawarō, yamamon, yamanto, yaman wakkashi (山の若い衆, "young person of the mountain") and yaman ojiyan (山の伯父やん, "mountain uncle"). In Kuma District in the same prefecture, they are also known as yaman-tarō (山ん太郎) or yamanbo (山ん坊). The kanji for yamawaro can also be written as 山𤢖 (yamawaro). The sansō (山𤢖) is the name of the Chinese yōkai that this comes from.

claims.statement: Yamawaro is a mountain yōkai reported in western Japan and Kyūshū.
claims.statement_id: Yamawaro adalah yōkai gunung yang diceritakan di Jepang barat dan Kyūshū.
claims.quote: Yamawaro (山童; or yamawarau) is a yōkai (spirit) said to appear in mountains in Western Japan, starting in the Kyūshū region.

claims.statement: Some stories identify it as a kappa living in the mountains.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian cerita menyebutnya kappa yang tinggal di gunung.
claims.quote: According to mythology, it is sometimes said that they are kappa that have come to dwell in the mountains.

claims.statement: The Wakan Sansai Zue places it deep in the mountains.
claims.statement_id: Wakan Sansai Zue menempatkannya jauh di pegunungan.
claims.quote: According to the Edo-period Wakan Sansai Zue, yamawaro lives in the depths of the mountains in Kyushu.

claims.statement: That book describes upright walking and human speech.
claims.statement_id: Buku itu menggambarkannya berjalan tegak dan berbicara seperti manusia.
claims.quote: The Wakan Sansai Zue states that yamawaro has a short torso, walks upright on two long legs, and speaks in human language.

claims.statement: A common depiction gives it one central eye.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran umum memberinya satu mata di tengah kepala.
claims.quote: A yamawaro’s most distinguishing feature is the single eye in the middle of its head.

claims.statement: It is said to imitate a variety of noises.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon mampu meniru beragam suara.
claims.quote: They are skillful mimics, copying the sound of falling rocks, wind, dynamite, and tools.

description.en: The Yato-no-kami (夜刀の神; "gods of the night-sword") are snake deities in Japanese folklore appearing in the Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki.

claims.statement: Yato-no-kami are Japanese snake deities recorded in the Hitachi Fudoki.
claims.statement_id: Yato-no-kami adalah dewa ular Jepang yang dicatat dalam Hitachi Fudoki.
claims.quote: The Yato-no-kami (夜刀の神; "gods of the night-sword") are snake deities in Japanese folklore appearing in the Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki.

claims.statement: The account places them in fields in Namegata county.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu menempatkan mereka di ladang daerah Namegata.
claims.quote: They lived in Namegata county, in fields near the government office.

claims.statement: They are associated with rough kami and the violent side of nature.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dikaitkan dengan kami garang dan sisi alam yang ganas.
claims.quote: As a snake, it was an araburu-kami (荒ぶる神; "rough, aggressive kami") which are fierce kami who represent the ferocious side of nature, such as raging rivers and fierce storms - as well as natural disasters.

claims.statement: Seeing them is rumored to bring destruction to a family.
claims.statement_id: Melihat mereka dikabarkan mendatangkan kehancuran keluarga.
claims.quote: Yato no kami were rumored to bring familial extermination on anyone who saw them.

claims.statement: Matachi is said to kill and enshrine them during Keitai’s reign.
claims.statement_id: Matachi konon membunuh dan memuja mereka pada masa Keitai.
claims.quote: It's told that Yato no Kami were killed and enshrined by a man named Yahazu no uji no Matachi during the time when Emperor Keitai was in reign.

claims.statement: A later account has Maro drive them away from construction workers.
claims.statement_id: Kisah selanjutnya menyebut Maro mengusir mereka dari para pekerja pembangunan.
claims.quote: The Yato no kami vanished later when a man named Mibunomuroji Maro drove them away from disturbing him and his workers who were building a moat there.

description.en: A Yekyua or "mother animal" is a class of Yakut spirits that remain hidden until the snow melts in the Spring. The Yakuts are a Turkic people. Each yekyua is associated with a particular animal. They act as familiar spirits to protect Yakut shamans. They are dangerous and powerful. The most dangerous are attached to female shamans. The type of animal determines the strength of the yekyua. For example, dog yekyua have little power, while elk yekyua do. Only shaman can see yekyua. When a shaman puts his/her spirit into his yekyua, he/she is dependent on his animal part. If another shaman who has manifested his animal kills the animal of another, the shaman with the dead animal dies. When the yekyua are fighting in the spring, the shaman with which they are associated feel ill. Dog yekyua are not prized as they gnaw at the shaman and destroy his body, bringing him sickness. Ordinarily, a good yekyua protects the shaman.

claims.statement: A Yekyua or "mother animal" is a class of Yakut spirits that stay hidden until the snow melts in spring.
claims.statement_id: Yekyua atau "hewan induk" adalah golongan roh Yakut yang bersembunyi sampai salju mencair pada musim semi.
claims.quote: A Yekyua or "mother animal" is a class of Yakut spirits that remain hidden until the snow melts in the Spring.

claims.statement: Each yekyua is tied to a particular animal and acts as a familiar spirit protecting Yakut shamans; they are dangerous and powerful, the most dangerous attached to female shamans.
claims.statement_id: Setiap yekyua terkait dengan seekor hewan tertentu dan menjadi roh pendamping yang melindungi dukun Yakut; mereka berbahaya dan kuat, dan yang paling berbahaya melekat pada dukun perempuan.
claims.quote: Each yekyua is associated with a particular animal. They act as familiar spirits to protect Yakut shamans. They are dangerous and powerful. The most dangerous are attached to female shamans.

claims.statement: The kind of animal sets a yekyua's strength: dog yekyua are weak, elk yekyua strong; only shamans can see yekyua.
claims.statement_id: Jenis hewan menentukan kekuatan yekyua: yekyua anjing lemah, sedangkan yekyua rusa elk kuat; hanya dukun yang dapat melihat yekyua.
claims.quote: The type of animal determines the strength of the yekyua. For example, dog yekyua have little power, while elk yekyua do. Only shaman can see yekyua.

claims.statement: If one shaman kills another's animal, the shaman whose animal died also dies.
claims.statement_id: Bila seorang dukun membunuh hewan dukun lain, dukun yang hewannya mati ikut meninggal.
claims.quote: If another shaman who has manifested his animal kills the animal of another, the shaman with the dead animal dies.

claims.statement: When the yekyua fight in spring, their shamans fall ill.
claims.statement_id: Saat para yekyua bertarung pada musim semi, dukun yang terkait dengannya jatuh sakit.
claims.quote: When the yekyua are fighting in the spring, the shaman with which they are associated feel ill.

claims.statement: The strongest yekyua is the mammoth.
claims.statement_id: Yekyua yang paling kuat adalah yekyua mamut.
claims.quote: Najsilniejszy jest yekuya - mamut.

description.id: Yeti adalah sejenis primata besar menyerupai manusia yang menghuni wilayah pegunungan Himalaya di Nepal dan Tibet. Nama Yeti dan Meh-Teh umumnya digunakan secara luas oleh penduduk asli di wilayah tersebut, dan merupakan bagian dari kisah sejarah dan mitologi mereka. Orang-orang Nepal juga menyebutnya Bonmanche yang berarti "manusia liar" atau "Kanchanjunga rachyyas" yang berarti "Iblis Kanchanjunga."
description.en: The Yeti (), also commonly referred to as the Abominable Snowman in Western popular culture, is a large, hairy, mythical humanoid creature said to inhabit the Himalayan mountain range in Asia. Many dubious articles have been offered in an attempt to prove the existence of the Yeti, including anecdotal visual sightings, disputed video recordings, photographs, and plaster casts of large footprints. Some of these are speculated or known to be hoaxes. Folklorists trace the origin of the Yeti to a combination of factors, including Sherpa folklore and misidentified fauna such as bear or yak. The Yeti is commonly compared to Bigfoot of North America as the two subjects often have similar physical descriptions.

claims.statement: Written accounts of the Tibetan Yeti legend date to the twelfth century.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Yeti dalam tradisi Tibet tercatat sejak abad ke-12.
claims.quote: Written accounts of the Tibetan legend of the Yeti date back to the 12th century.

claims.statement: Some accounts portray the yeti as a reddish-brown-haired, ape-like biped.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah menggambarkan Yeti sebagai sosok mirip kera berbulu cokelat kemerahan yang berjalan dengan dua kaki.
claims.quote: Also called a "wild man," many accounts describe the creature as an ape-like being, over six feet tall, walking on its back legs, with reddish-brown fur covering its muscular body.

claims.statement: Tibetan tradition has two-legged yetis and larger four-legged ones said to prey on livestock.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi Tibet mengenal variasi Yeti berkaki dua dan bentuk lebih besar berkaki empat yang memangsa ternak.
claims.quote: Tibetan tradition recognizes a variety of Yeti, one said to walk on two legs, and another larger Yeti that preys on livestock and walks on four legs.

claims.statement: In the stories, yetis are believed to inhabit alpine forests below the snow line.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita, Yeti dipercaya menghuni hutan alpin di bawah garis salju.
claims.quote: Yeti are believed to live in the alpine forest below the snow line, although they will brave higher altitude for food and shelter.

claims.statement: In many stories, the yeti is nocturnal and makes a high-pitched whistle or screech.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak cerita, Yeti aktif pada malam hari dan mengeluarkan siulan atau jeritan bernada tinggi.
claims.quote: In many stories, the Yeti is nocturnal, and emits a high-pitched screech or whistle.

claims.statement: Tibetan Buddhist stories feature both kind and malevolent yetis.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Buddhis Tibet, Yeti dapat tampil baik ataupun jahat.
claims.quote: Tibetan Buddhist stories feature Yetis as both kind and malevolent characters.

claims.statement: The white-furred film depiction lacks folkloric support before the twentieth century.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran Yeti berbulu putih yang lazim dalam film tidak didukung cerita rakyat sebelum abad ke-20.
claims.quote: But there's no real folklore that supports that version before the 20th century.

claims.statement: Mitochondrial DNA analysis of purported yeti samples supported their identification as local bears.
claims.statement_id: Analisis DNA mitokondria atas sampel yang diklaim sebagai Yeti mendukung identifikasi sampel itu sebagai beruang lokal.
claims.quote: Phylogenetic analyses of mitochondrial DNA sequences determined clade affinities of the purported yeti samples in this study, strongly supporting the biological basis of the yeti legend to be local, extant bears.

claims.statement: Researchers associate the yeti legend with local bears while acknowledging uncertainty around the wider stories.
claims.statement_id: Kajian ilmiah mengaitkan kisah Yeti dengan beruang setempat, tetapi identitas seluruh kisah tentang sosok mirip manusia tetap diperdebatkan.
claims.quote: Although anecdotally associated with local bears (Ursus arctos and U. thibetanus), the exact identity of ‘hominid’-like creatures important to folklore and mythology in the Tibetan Plateau–Himalaya region is still surrounded by mystery.

claims.statement: Reports of purported yeti footprints spurred Western climbers' interest in the 1950s.
claims.statement_id: Laporan jejak yang diklaim sebagai Yeti memicu minat pendaki Barat pada 1950-an.
claims.quote: Believed by some to live in the Himalayan Mountains, interest in the Yeti spiked during the 1950s, when Western climbers ascending Mount Everest reported Yeti footprints.

claims.statement: Nepal issued rules for yeti-seeking expeditions.
claims.statement_id: Pemerintah Nepal pernah mengeluarkan aturan bagi ekspedisi pencarian Yeti.
claims.quote: This prompted the government of Nepal to issue regulations for Yeti-hunting expeditions

description.id: Yosuzume (Jepang: 夜雀) disebut juga dengan nama Tamoto Suzume atau Okuri Suzume adalah yokai berwujud burung langka yang tersebar di Pulau Shikoku. Yokai ini muncul pada malam hari dalam bentuk kawanan besar yang berisik dan sering melewati jalan-jalan terpencil atau jalan di sektar pegunungan. Yosuzume lebih menyukai muncul di hadapan para pelancong, berputar-putar di sekitar mereka dalam gerombolan yang menyeramkan. Di beberapa tempat, yosuzume dikenal dengan sebutan tamoto suzume dan kemunculannya disertai dengan serigala, anjing hutan, atau yokai lain. Suara bising mereka hanya dapat terdengar oleh satu orang dan kemungkinan orang tersebut akan mendapatkan kesialan.
description.en: Yosuzume (夜雀, "Night-Sparrow") are bird yōkai, the knowledge of which is handed down within the Hada District, Aichi Prefecture towns of Tanokuchi (presently Kuroshio), Tomiyama (presently Nakamura), in Kitagawa, Aki District, in Minamiuwa District, Ehime Prefecture, and in other places.

claims.statement: Yosuzume are bird yōkai known as night sparrows.
claims.statement_id: Yosuzume adalah yōkai burung yang disebut burung pipit malam.
claims.quote: Yosuzume (夜雀, "Night-Sparrow") are bird yōkai

claims.statement: They appear at night and chirp like sparrows on mountain trails.
claims.statement_id: Mereka muncul malam hari dan berkicau seperti burung pipit di jalur pegunungan.
claims.quote: As indicated by their name, they are a yōkai that appear in the night and chirp "chi, chi, chi" like a sparrow, and are said to pass in front of people who walk along mountain trails.

claims.statement: One belief says catching them causes night blindness.
claims.statement_id: Satu kepercayaan menyebut penangkapan burung itu menyebabkan rabun senja.
claims.quote: Also, it is said that if one carelessly caught them, then one gets afflicted with nyctalopia.

claims.statement: In Wakayama, their presence can indicate a protective wolf.
claims.statement_id: Di Wakayama, keberadaannya dapat menandakan serigala pelindung.
claims.quote: In reverse, in Wakayama Prefecture, they were not bad luck, and while possessed by a night sparrow, it was proof that a wolf was giving protection from the monsters of the mountain.

claims.statement: Other accounts interpret their presence as bad luck.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menafsirkan keberadaan mereka sebagai pertanda sial.
claims.quote: By themselves they don’t do any particular harm other than startling people; however they are a sign of very bad luck and are thought to bring terrible evil to those whom they swarm around.

claims.statement: A regional account says only one traveler in a group hears their call.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah daerah menyebut hanya satu pelancong dalam kelompok yang mendengar suaranya.
claims.quote: Their call is mysteriously only ever heard by a single individual, even when traveling in groups.

description.en: Ysbaddaden Bencawr; "Ysbaddaden, Chief of Giants" (from roots meaning "hawthorn" or "infertile" - or perhaps implying both meanings), is the primary antagonist of the Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen. A vicious giant residing in a nigh unreachable castle, he is the father of Olwen and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin.

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden Bencawr, Chief of Giants, is the antagonist of the Welsh Culhwch and Olwen, a vicious giant, father of Olwen and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr, Kepala Para Raksasa (hawthorn/mandul), antagonis Culhwch and Olwen (Wales, Welsh), raksasa kejam, ayah Olwen, paman Goreu fab Custennin; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Ysbaddaden Bencawr ; "Ysbaddaden, Chief of Giants" (from roots meaning "hawthorn" or "infertile" - or perhaps implying both meanings), is the primary antagonist of the Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen. A vicious giant residing in a nigh unreachable castle, he is the father of Olwen and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin.

claims.statement: His stepmother curses Culhwch to marry only Olwen; he seeks Arthur.
claims.statement_id: Ibu tiri mengutuk Culhwch agar hanya menikahi Olwen; ia mencari Arthur.
claims.quote: Offended, the new queen puts a curse on him so that he can marry no one besides the beautiful Olwen, daughter of the giant Ysbaddaden.

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden took Custennin's lands and killed his twenty-three children.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden merampas tanah Custennin dan membunuh dua puluh tiga anaknya.
claims.quote: They learn that the castle belongs to Ysbaddaden, that he stripped Custennin of his lands and murdered the shepherd's twenty-three children out of cruelty.

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden tries to kill Culhwch with a poison dart, wounded by Bedwyr, Menw and Culhwch; sets impossible tasks (anoethau) including Twrch Trwyth.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden mencoba membunuh Culhwch dengan anak panah beracun, dilukai Bedwyr, Menw, Culhwch; memberi tugas mustahil (anoethau) termasuk Twrch Trwyth.
claims.quote: Upon their arrival, Ysbaddaden attempts to kill Culhwch with a poison dart, but is outwitted and wounded, first by Bedwyr, then by the enchanter Menw, and finally by Culhwch himself. Eventually, Ysbaddaden relents, and agrees to give Culhwch his daughter on the condition that he complete a number of impossible tasks (anoethau), including hunting the Twrch Trwy

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden Bencawr/Pengawyr in Welsh (walisischen) myth is a chief giant (Oberriese); his castle has nine gates (neun Toren); father of Olwen.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr/Pengawyr dalam mitologi Wales (walisischen) Oberriese, raksasa utama; kastel sembilan gerbang (neun Toren); ayah Olwen.
claims.quote: auch Ysbaddaden Pengawyr, ist in der walisischen Mythologie ein „Oberriese“ oder „Hauptriese“ (bencawr, pengawyr). Er besitzt eine Burg mit neun Toren und ist der Vater von Olwen, der Bruder des riesigen Schäfers Custenhin und der Onkel von Goreu.

claims.statement: His heavy eyelids (Augenlider) are lifted by a servant with a fork (Gabel); compare Balor.
claims.statement_id: Kelopak mata (Augenlider) berat diangkat pelayan dengan garpu (Gabel); bandingkan Balor.
claims.quote: Ysbaddaden hat Augenlider, die so schwer sind, dass sie ein Diener mit der Gabel hochheben muss, wenn er jemanden betrachten will (vergleiche dazu Balor).

description.id: Yume no seirei (Jepang: 夢の精霊) adalah yokai misterius dalam cerita rakyat Jepang yang diyakini sebagai penyebab munculnya mimpi buruk.
description.en: Yume no seirei (夢の精霊, "dream spirit") is a mysterious yōkai in Japanese mythology, believed to cause nightmares.

claims.statement: Yume no seirei is a Japanese dream spirit associated with nightmares.
claims.statement_id: Yume no seirei adalah roh mimpi Jepang yang terkait dengan mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: Yume no seirei (夢の精霊, "dream spirit") is a mysterious yōkai in Japanese mythology, believed to cause nightmares.

claims.statement: Sawaki Suushi’s 1737 Hyakkai Zukan includes this figure.
claims.statement_id: Hyakkai Zukan karya Sawaki Suushi tahun 1737 memuat sosok ini.
claims.quote: He appears in the Hyakkai zukan (Illustrated volume of a hundred demons) created by Sawaki Sūshi in 1737.

claims.statement: The figure has the appearance of a very thin old man.
claims.statement_id: Sosok ini berwujud lelaki tua sangat kurus.
claims.quote: Artists depict yume no seirei as an emaciated, elderly man.

claims.statement: His loose white clothing leaves the ribs visible.
claims.statement_id: Pakaian putihnya yang longgar membiarkan rusuk terlihat.
claims.quote: He wears a loose white robe, which reveals his frail body and exposed ribcage.

claims.statement: He has flowing sparse hair.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki rambut jarang yang terurai.
claims.quote: His thin wispy hair flows behind him in a ghostly motion.

claims.statement: He carries a cane and beckons with his other hand.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa tongkat dan melambaikan tangan lainnya.
claims.quote: In his right hand he holds a cane and with his left he reaches out, beckoning.

claims.statement: His lower body appears to fade away.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh bagian bawahnya tampak memudar.
claims.quote: The bottom half of his body eerily fades away as if he is disappearing.

description.en: A žaltys (Lithuanian pronunciation: [ʒɐlʲˈtʲǐːs], literally: grass snake) is a household spirit in Lithuanian mythology. It is a sacred animal of the sun goddess Saulė, and was considered a guardian of the home and a symbol of fertility. People used to keep it as a pet by the stove or other special area of the house, believing that it would bring good harvest and wealth. Killing the žaltys was said to bring great misfortunes upon the household. If a žaltys was found in the field, people gave it milk attempting to befriend the creature and make it a sacred household pet.

claims.statement: The žaltys (grass snake) is a household spirit of Lithuanian mythology, sacred animal of the sun goddess Saulė, guardian of the home and symbol of fertility; people kept it by the stove believing it brought good harvests and wealth; killing it brought misfortune; one found in a field was given milk.
claims.statement_id: Žaltys (ular rumput) adalah roh rumah dalam mitologi Lituania, binatang suci dewi matahari Saulė, penjaga rumah dan lambang kesuburan; orang memeliharanya di dekat tungku dan percaya ia membawa panen baik dan kekayaan; membunuhnya mendatangkan malapetaka; bila ditemukan di ladang ia diberi susu.
claims.quote: is a household spirit in Lithuanian mythology. It is a sacred animal of the sun goddess Saulė, and was considered a guardian of the home and a symbol of fertility. People used to keep it as a pet by the stove or other special area of the house, believing that it would bring good harvest and wealth. Killing the žaltys was said to bring great misfortunes upon the household.

claims.statement: There is a story of a young woman named Eglė who found a žaltys in her clothes after bathing in a lake; it offered to return them if she married it; she agreed, and the žaltys, Žilvinas, King of the Grass Snakes, became a handsome young man and her husband.
claims.statement_id: Ada kisah gadis bernama Eglė yang menemukan žaltys di pakaiannya setelah mandi di danau; ular itu berjanji mengembalikan pakaiannya bila ia mau menikahinya; Eglė setuju, dan žaltys itu, Žilvinas, Raja Ular Rumput, menjelma pemuda tampan menjadi suaminya.
claims.quote: There is a story of a young women named Eglė who found a žaltys in her clothes after she bathed in a lake. He spoke to her and said he would give her back her clothes if she married him. She eventually agreed, and later the žaltys, who was King of the Grass Snakes Žilvinas, would take the form of a handsome young man to become her husband.

claims.statement: He took her to his undersea home, where she became immortal as Queen of the Grass Snakes.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa Eglė ke rumahnya di bawah laut, tempat Eglė menjadi abadi sebagai Ratu Ular Rumput.
claims.quote: He took her to his undersea home where she became immortal as Queen of the Grass Snakes.

claims.statement: The žaltys was considered a messenger of the gods and the Sun's favourite, so killing it was a crime; a Lithuanian proverb says "At the sight of a dead grass snake even the Sun weeps".
claims.statement_id: Žaltys dianggap utusan para dewa dan kesayangan Matahari, sehingga membunuhnya disamakan dengan kejahatan; pepatah Lituania berkata "Melihat ular rumput mati, Matahari pun menangis".
claims.quote: Жалтис считался посланцем богов, любимцем Солнца, потому убийство Жалтиса приравнивалось к преступлению. В литовском языке существует пословица: «При виде мёртвого ужа и Солнце плачет».

claims.statement: The žaltys (Latvian Zalktis) is a deity in the form of a grass snake in Latvian and Lithuanian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Žaltys (Latvia: Zalktis) adalah dewa berwujud ular rumput dalam mitologi Latvia dan Lituania.
claims.quote: божество в образе ужа в латышской и литовской мифологии.

claims.statement: The žaltys was considered a protector of livestock and compared with Piena Māte (the Milk Mother).
claims.statement_id: Žaltys dianggap pelindung ternak dan dibandingkan dengan Piena Māte (Ibu Susu).
claims.quote: Жальтис считался покровителем скота и сравнивается с Piena Māte (Молочная мать).

description.id: Zashiki warashi (座敷童子) adalah arwah anak-anak yang terutama dipercaya penduduk Prefektur Iwate, Jepang. Arwah ini dipercaya sebagai kami (dewa), yang tinggal di zashiki atau gudang; warashi berarti anak-anak. Menurut cerita rakyat Jepang, zashiki warashi mendatangkan kekayaan untuk rumah yang ditinggalinya. Meskipun ia suka mengusili anggota keluarga yang tinggal di rumah itu, tetapi akan mendatangkan keberuntungan kepada anggota keluarga yang dapat melihatnya. Cerita zashiki warashi menjadi populer setelah Kunio Yanagita menerbitkan kumpulan cerita legenda Tōno Monogatari (Hikayat dari Tōno) dan Ishigami Mondō (Tanya Jawab mengenai Ishigami). Salah satu kamar di penginapan Ryokufoso yang berada di Ninohe, Prefektur Iwate dipercaya ditinggali oleh zashiki warashi. Penginapan ini telah berulang kali dijadikan bahan liputan media massa, termasuk acara televisi di Jepang.
description.en: Zashiki-warashi (座敷童子; or 座敷童, "parlor child"), sometimes also called zashiki bokko (座敷ぼっこ; "parlor boyo"), are spirit-like beings told about mostly in the Iwate Prefecture. They are said to be yokai that live in parlors or storage rooms, and that they perform pranks. It is believed that people who saw one would receive good fortune. There are also legends of how they would bring fortune to families. They are also known from Kunio Yanagita's Tōno Monogatari, Ishigami Mondō, and stories about them appear in the 17th and 18th chapters of the Tōno Monogatari and the 87th chapter titled "Zashiki-warashi" of the Tōno Monogatari Shūi. In the 17th chapter, it is written "families with whom this spirit dwells become prosperous" (kono kami no yadoritamafu ihe ha fūki jizai nari to ifu koto nari).

claims.statement: Zashiki-warashi is described as a household deity that looks like a child.
claims.statement_id: Zashiki-warashi digambarkan sebagai dewa rumah berwujud anak.
claims.quote: The zashiki-warashi, a household deity that looks like a child

claims.statement: The Tōno stories come from mountainous Iwate.
claims.statement_id: Cerita Tōno berasal dari wilayah pegunungan Iwate.
claims.quote: The Tōno region, nestled amid the mountains of Iwate Prefecture in northern Japan, is famous for its folktales.

claims.statement: Another account places this child spirit in rooms or storehouses.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menempatkan roh anak ini di kamar atau gudang.
claims.quote: The Zashiki-warashi is a child spirit that is said to reside in rooms or storehouses.

claims.statement: Homes with zashiki-warashi are believed to thrive.
claims.statement_id: Rumah yang dihuni zashiki-warashi dipercaya makmur.
claims.quote: It is believed that homes with a Zashiki-warashi will thrive

claims.statement: Its departure is believed to bring poverty.
claims.statement_id: Kepergiannya dipercaya membuat keluarga miskin.
claims.quote: while those from which it leaves will become poor.

claims.statement: An Iwate guide calls it a boy-shaped guardian spirit of the house.
claims.statement_id: Pemandu Iwate menyebut roh pelindung rumah berwujud anak lelaki.
claims.quote: Zashikiwarashi is not a ghost, but a divine spirit of a boy with a cute bobbed hair, and in this region it is considered an important guardian deity of the house.

claims.statement: Yanagita Kunio published the Tōno story collection in 1910.
claims.statement_id: Yanagita Kunio menerbitkan kumpulan kisah Tōno pada 1910.
claims.quote: The original Tōno monogatari [trans. The Legends of Tōno] was published in 1910 by folklorist Yanagita Kunio, collecting stories gathered by Sasaki Kizen, a Tōno native himself.

claims.statement: An inn says the spirit lives in Enju-no-Ma and that those who see it succeed.
claims.statement_id: Penginapan menyebut ruang Enju-no-Ma tempat roh itu tinggal dan menjanjikan sukses bagi yang melihatnya.
claims.quote: At the end of a long corridor is the "Enju-no-Ma," a room where the Zashiki Warashi live, and it is said that those who see them will be successful in life.

claims.statement: The tourism guide reports claimed sightings while calling it a legend.
claims.statement_id: Bahan wisata menyebut klaim penampakan, sambil menegaskan ini legenda.
claims.quote: Although it is a legend, there are still many people who claim to have seen the Zashiki Warashi.

description.en: Zhulong or Zhuyin , also known in English as the Torch Dragon, was a giant red solar dragon and god in Chinese mythology. It supposedly had a human's face and snake's body, created day and night by opening and closing its eyes, and created seasonal winds by breathing.

claims.statement: Zhulong is a giant red dragon and solar deity in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Zhulong adalah naga merah raksasa dan dewa matahari dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Zhulong /ˈdʒuːlɒŋ/ or Zhuyin /ˈdʒuːjɪn/, also known in English as the Torch Dragon, was a giant red solar dragon and god in Chinese mythology. It supposedly had a human's face and snake's body, created day and night by opening and closing its eyes, and created seasonal winds by breathing.

claims.statement: He is portrayed with a human face and a serpent's body.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan berwajah manusia dan bertubuh ular.
claims.quote: Zhulong /ˈdʒuːlɒŋ/ or Zhuyin /ˈdʒuːjɪn/, also known in English as the Torch Dragon, was a giant red solar dragon and god in Chinese mythology. It supposedly had a human's face and snake's body, created day and night by opening and closing its eyes, and created seasonal winds by breathing.

claims.statement: Opening and closing his eyes produces day and night, while breathing produces seasonal winds.
claims.statement_id: Membuka dan menutup matanya menciptakan siang dan malam, sedangkan napasnya menciptakan angin musim.
claims.quote: Zhulong /ˈdʒuːlɒŋ/ or Zhuyin /ˈdʒuːjɪn/, also known in English as the Torch Dragon, was a giant red solar dragon and god in Chinese mythology. It supposedly had a human's face and snake's body, created day and night by opening and closing its eyes, and created seasonal winds by breathing.

claims.statement: The Chu Ci contains name variants Chuolong and Zhuolong.
claims.statement_id: Chu Ci memuat varian nama Chuolong dan Zhuolong.
claims.quote: In the Chu Ci, Zhulong is also rendered as Chuolong, which can variously mean "Distant" or "Quarrelsome Dragon", and as Zhuolong, variously "Outstanding" or "Departed Dragon". According to present reconstructions, these variant characters 逴 (now chuò) and 趠 (now zhuó) sounded closer to the pronunciation of 燭 in old Chinese, although not homophonous.

claims.statement: The names Zhuyin and Zhulong occur in Han-period classical texts.
claims.statement_id: Nama Zhuyin dan Zhulong ditemukan dalam teks klasik zaman Han.
claims.quote: The names "Zhuyin" and "Zhulong" appear in classic Chinese texts from the Han (3rd century BCE – 3rd century CE) that record the myths of the Zhou (12th–3rd century BCE).

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing gives parallel accounts of Zhuyin and Zhulong.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing memberikan kisah sejajar mengenai Zhuyin dan Zhulong.
claims.quote: The Classic of Mountains and Seas (c. 3rd century BCE - 1st century CE) records parallel myths about Zhuyin and Zhulong.

description.en: Zmei m. (Russian: змей, zmej) and zmeya f. (змея́, zmejá), meaning "serpent", is a form of dragon in Russian folktales and epic poetry; sometimes, a human-like character with dragon-like traits. Two of the most famous zmei are Gorynych and Tugarin, two well-known zmei, appear as adversaries of the bogatyri (heroes) Dobrynya Nikitich or Alyosha Popovich.

claims.statement: Zmei (masculine) and zmeya (feminine), meaning "serpent", is a form of dragon in Russian folktales and epic poetry, sometimes a human-like character with dragon traits.
claims.statement_id: Zmei (laki-laki, змей) dan zmeya (perempuan), yang berarti "ular", adalah bentuk naga dalam dongeng dan epos Rusia, kadang tokoh mirip manusia bersifat naga.
claims.quote: meaning "serpent", is a form of dragon in Russian folktales and epic poetry; sometimes, a human-like character with dragon-like traits.

claims.statement: The two most famous zmei, Gorynych and Tugarin, appear as adversaries of the bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich or Alyosha Popovich.
claims.statement_id: Dua zmei paling terkenal adalah Gorynych dan Tugarin, lawan para bogatyr Dobrynya Nikitich atau Alyosha Popovich.
claims.quote: Two of the most famous zmei are Gorynych and Tugarin, two well-known zmei, appear as adversaries of the bogatyri (heroes) Dobrynya Nikitich or Alyosha Popovich.

claims.statement: Another form is zmiy, borrowed from Church Slavonic.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk lain adalah zmiy, serapan dari bahasa Slavonik Gereja.
claims.quote: Another form is zmiy (змий, zmij), borrowed from Church Slavonic

claims.statement: Despite meaning serpent, when used of dragons zmei always implies the flying kind all over Russia.
claims.statement_id: Walau berarti ular, bila merujuk naga istilah zmei di seluruh Rusia selalu menyiratkan jenis yang terbang.
claims.quote: Despite meaning serpent, when referring to dragons, the term zmei always implicitly refers to the flying kind all over Russia.

claims.statement: Zmey Gorynych is a Russian folk dragon who abducts women; he usually lives in the mountains, often by a fiery river, guarding the Kalinov Bridge to the realm of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Zmey Gorynych adalah naga cerita rakyat Rusia yang menculik perempuan; ia biasanya tinggal di pegunungan, sering dekat sungai api, dan menjaga Jembatan Kalinov menuju alam orang mati.
claims.quote: Змей Горы́ныч — русский фольклорный змей (дракон), похищающий женщин. Змей Горыныч обитает обычно в горах, нередко у огненной реки и стережёт «Калинов мост», по которому попадают в царство мёртвых.

claims.statement: Many heads are the Zmey's constant trait, usually multiples of three (3, 6, 9, 12); most often three-headed; he usually flies but his wings are rarely mentioned; in Afanasyev's whole collection "fiery wings" appear only once.
claims.statement_id: Kepala banyak adalah ciri tetap Zmey, biasanya kelipatan tiga (3, 6, 9, 12); paling sering berkepala tiga; umumnya dapat terbang tetapi sayapnya jarang disebut; dalam seluruh kumpulan dongeng Afanasyev "sayap api" hanya disebut sekali.
claims.quote: Многоголовость Змея — непременная его черта. Число голов обычно кратно трём, чаще всего их бывает 3, 6, 9 или 12 ... Чаще всего Змей предстаёт трёхглавым. ... В большинстве случаев у Змея отмечается способность к полёту, но о крыльях его, как правило, ничего не говорится. Так, во всём сборнике русских народных сказок Александра Афанасьева лишь один раз сообщается об «огненных крыльях»
